title: Supply Chain Lead, Amazon Key
descriptionHtml:
As a Supply Chain Lead within the Smart TDR (STDR) Program, you will own end-to-end supply chain planning and execution for Amazon's Smart Trailer Dock and Retrieval technology deployment across the NA fulfillment network. You will have a holistic view of material procurement, vendor operations, and installation logistics across NASC, DC, and CH networks — and be integral in driving large-scale initiatives in material cost optimization, vendor management, PO reconciliation, and installation capacity planning. With a deployment target spanning thousands of doors across multiple networks and fiscal years, there will rarely be a perfect solution — it will be up to you to make data-driven decisions and manage complex vendor and cross-functional stakeholder relationships while planning and executing within a rapidly evolving program.

The Supply Chain Lead will work in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment — coordinating across hardware engineering, installation vendors, field operations, finance, and procurement teams — and communicate business conditions and program decisions effectively across multiple levels, from vendor field technicians to Amazon Directors and VPs. In this role, you will seek out supply chain gaps, dive deep into PO and invoice data, earn trust of partner teams, and deliver results that influence program-level financial outcomes. This role blends short-term execution (weekly install schedules, PO tracking, vendor invoicing) with long-term strategic planning (cost-per-door optimization, vendor negotiation strategy, surplus disposition), requiring quick decision-making with incomplete data while also thinking big about the network-wide deployment roadmap. The end goal is to answer the question: how do we deploy STDR technology across Amazon's network faster, at lower cost per door, with zero material waste, and without impacting site operations.



Key job responsibilities
Key Job Responsibilities
Demonstrate strong customer focus and ownership of program-level supply chain outcomes
Own end-to-end material planning: demand forecasting against install targets, PO management, vendor coordination, and surplus reconciliation
Drive cross-network PO visibility and reconciliation across NASC, DC, CH, and Pilot programs — ensuring single source of truth for spend and utilization
Lead vendor negotiations (panel sub-vendors, contract manufacturers, GDO suppliers) to optimize cost, manage surplus, and maintain strategic relationships
Identify, prioritize, and implement processes to eliminate supply chain defects — including PO deduplication, invoicing gaps, and untracked cross-network procurement
Execute thorough root cause analysis on cost variances and deliver data-backed recommendations to senior leadership
Own programmatic execution at both detailed (weekly PO tracking, invoice validation) and strategic levels (cost-per-door targets, multi-year material strategy)
Successfully operate and influence in a cross-functional capacity across hardware, operations, finance, and procurement
Data mine by leveraging SQL/Python to drive key business decisions on material utilization, surplus disposition, and cost optimization
Basic Qualifications
5+ years of program or project management experience
5+ years of supply chain experience, preferably in hardware deployment, construction, or technology installation programs
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end-to-end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
Experience managing vendor relationships and purchase order lifecycles at scale

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of program or project management experience
- 3+ years of working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams experience
- 3+ years of defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics experience
- 2+ years of supply chain experience
- Bachelor's degree
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership experience
- 3+ years of driving process improvements experience
- Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
- Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

descriptionHtml:
Amazon has an immediate opening for a Senior Program Manager to join our Finance and Business Integration team.

This position supports and can directly influence the launches of some of Amazon’s newest global business initiatives in the Prime Video organization. This leader will work closely with the global financial systems team, accounting operations teams, tax, treasury, and others and represent the accounting organization to various stakeholders. In this role, the candidate will be part of a team that collaborates with business finance and technical teams to deliver world class solutions that are highly scalable, secure, and flexible. title: Sr PM, Damage Stds, Worldwide Returns & ReCommerce
descriptionHtml:
In this role, you will own the Damage Standards Program, the objective criteria used to assess returned items and determine their eligibility for resale. Working at the intersection of customer experience, associate experience, grading accuracy, and returns economics, you will protect the customer experience, reduce concessions, and maintain customer trust across an increasingly complex product catalog. You will translate customer and field research into evaluation standards, partner with product managers, program managers, tech teams, science teams, and operations stakeholders, and drive continuous improvement across the returns network. You will own the standards that every downstream evaluation and recovery channel.

Key job responsibilities
• Own and continuously refine the damage standards across the returns network, working backwards from customer expectations.
• Drive a customer-centric feedback loop through customer focus groups, associate interviews, and field surveys, translating findings into validated standard revisions.
• Own the assessment framework and customer-experience risk categorizations.
• Act on calibration audit findings to improve grading accuracy on the lowest-performing evaluation attributes.
• Partner with product and operations teams to feed refined standards into product-specific evaluation and downstream recovery channels.
• Track key performance indicators (concession impact, customer experience, grading accuracy), supporting business reviews, senior leadership reviews, and weekly status updates.
• Lead cross-functional communication for standard updates, grading rule changes, and accuracy improvement initiatives across Operations, Product, Engineering, and research partners.
• Identify and mitigate risks, including accuracy degradation during transitions and customer experience risks.
• Own program goals and annual planning narrative contributions.

A day in the life
• Partner with business, research, and technical teams across the company, from site operations to applied science to product teams.
• Translate customer expectations and field research into objective, actionable evaluation standards.
• Develop scalable solutions for complex grading problems (e.g., product-specific damage criteria, attribute-level accuracy, customer-experience risk mapping).
• Conduct deep dives on concession drivers, grading accuracy, and calibration audit results, translating data into actionable mechanisms.
• Drive end-to-end program delivery and results, owning standards from research through controlled pilots through sustained performance.

About the team
We are a diverse team who:
- Embrace different perspectives and experiences
- Celebrate wins and accomplishments
- Are backed by strong leadership dedicated to operational excellence

Basic qualifications

- 6+ years of program or project management experience
- Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
- Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Master's degree
- 6+ years of Business strategy or Non-Tech Program Management experience
- Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
- 4+ years of developing program strategies and plans, diving execution, and influencing senior stakeholders experience
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams

Preferred qualifications

title: Value Engineering Manager, Value Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Amazon builds fast—and behind every new Fulfillment Center, Sortation Center, Delivery Station, and capital investment is a critical question: **Are we buying the right solution at the right price?** We're looking for a **Cost & Value Engineering Manager** to partner with Amazon's North America Design & Construction stakeholders, delivering construction cost engineering and value engineering services that optimize design, validate costs, and inform capital investment decisions across Amazon's infrastructure network.

This role is high-impact, high-variety, and technically demanding. You'll develop bottom-up cost estimates, should-cost models, and Value Engineering analyses across a diverse portfolio of building types, material handling equipment (MHE), automation, and capital projects. From multi-site retrofit programs to complex, one-off initiatives, you'll evaluate design alternatives, optimize specifications, identify cost drivers, and produce defensible cost models that shape sourcing, design, and investment decisions. Working from early concepts through bid-ready construction documents, you'll apply technical expertise to balance cost, quality, performance, and operational requirements.

As part of Amazon's Global Procurement Organization within the Sourcing Excellence pillar, you'll partner closely with Engineering, Design, Construction, Procurement, and Category teams to ensure Amazon is buying the right solution at the right price. You'll also collaborate with AI and Market Intelligence Solutions, leveraging AI-powered tools to accelerate analysis, develop scalable cost intelligence, and advance next-generation automation that expands the reach and impact of Cost & Value Engineering across Amazon.

Key job responsibilities
Deliver independent, bottom-up cost estimates for construction, equipment, and capital investment projects across Amazon's global portfolio, spanning retrofit, expansion, new-build, automation, and equipment deployment initiatives.
Develop cost estimates from early-stage concepts through supplier selection and implementation, adapting methodologies and analytical depth to available project information and design maturity.
Build and maintain scalable estimating models and templates while developing detailed bottom-up cost models for complex, site-specific initiatives requiring advanced analytical judgment.
Perform should-cost modeling, benchmarking, and Value Engineering analyses to evaluate design alternatives, optimize specifications, identify cost drivers, and ensure Amazon is buying the right solution at the right price.
Leverage AI-powered tools to automate data gathering, cost modeling, benchmarking, and pattern recognition while applying engineering judgment to validate outputs and resolve complex or ambiguous scopes.
Drive the development of scalable AI-enabled cost intelligence solutions by curating project and market data, validating model performance, and identifying opportunities to automate routine analytical activities.
Partner with Engineering, Design, Construction, Procurement, Category Management, and business stakeholders to validate assumptions, communicate cost risks, evaluate alternatives, and influence sourcing and investment decisions.
Peer review cost models, estimates, and Value Engineering recommendations to ensure technical rigor, consistency, and alignment with current market conditions and best practices.

About the team
The Sourcing Excellence team helps Amazon answer two fundamental questions: **Are we buying the right product?** (Value Engineering) and **Are we paying the right price?** (Cost Engineering). **Value Engineering** ensures Amazon is investing in the right construction solutions, equipment, and technologies by optimizing specifications, design, materials, and performance to maximize business value while meeting operational requirements. **Cost Engineering** establishes cost transparency and price confidence through bottom-up cost estimation, should-cost modeling, benchmarking, market intelligence, and cost driver analysis to determine what construction projects, equipment, and services should cost.

Together, these disciplines provide transparent, fact-based insights that enable informed sourcing, design, and investment decisions throughout the project lifecycle. Our vision is to make cost and value transparency a strategic capability across the organization, ensuring every investment delivers the optimal balance of cost, quality, performance, and operational requirements. Today, the team supports billions of dollars in managed spend across construction, material handling equipment, automation, and other strategic sourcing categories, and continues to scale its impact through AI-enabled solutions, standardized mechanisms, and cross-functional partnerships.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Knowledge of Excel (Pivot Tables, VLookUps) at an advanced level and SQL
- Experience in program or project management
- Experience working cross functionally with tech and non-tech teams
- Experience in defining and implementing process improvement initiatives using data and metrics
- Experience in supply chain
- Experience defining program requirements and using data and metrics to determine improvements

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in driving end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
- Experience leading process improvements
- Experience in stakeholder management, dealing with multiple stakeholders at varied levels of the organization
- Experience building processes, project management, and schedules

title: Principal Product Mgr - Tech, Ontology
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Catalog Ontology is the shared product-knowledge layer that powers experiences across the entire Stores ecosystem. Every time a customer searches, browses, or buys, structured product knowledge is working behind the scenes to deliver accurate discovery, trustworthy information, and broad selection. This is the first time the ontology is getting a dedicated Principal Product Manager - Technical to treat it as a product in its own right. You will define the product strategy from the ground up, drive adoption across the downstream domains that depend on it, and shape a roadmap whose benefits compound across the Stores business. If you are a technical product leader who does your best work in ambiguous, cross-organizational spaces and wants to own a problem where one good decision makes dozens of teams more effective, we want to talk to you.

Key job responsibilities
Own the end-to-end product vision and multi-year roadmap for the Catalog Ontology, treating it as a shared platform product consumed across all Amazon Stores surface areas.
Develop and drive an adoption strategy that gets downstream consumers — Shopping CX, Listing Ingestion, Fulfillment Systems, and beyond — to build on the ontology, producing the narratives, mechanisms, and reporting that lower the barrier to adoption.
Define and continuously improve the metrics that measure ontology adoption, data quality, and downstream customer impact, and use that data to inform trade-off decisions between long-term ontology investments and immediate consumer-team needs.
Influence engineering and science partners on schema-modeling decisions, ontology structure, and knowledge-graph architecture so the ontology scales across the Stores business and supports emerging AI and personalization experiences.
Partner across downstream domains and senior leadership to deliver a coherent, well-adopted product rather than point solutions, building consensus across organizations that each have their own priorities.

A day in the life
You might start by reviewing adoption and data-quality metrics, then shift into writing or refining a product narrative that explains the ontology's value to a new downstream team. Midday could bring a technical design review with engineering and science partners, where you evaluate schema-modeling trade-offs — how a change to an ontology class or constraint rule will ripple across multiple surfaces. Later, you may meet with senior leaders across Shopping CX, Listing Ingestion, or Fulfillment to align on shared goals and unblock cross-org dependencies. Growth here comes through expanding the scope and ambiguity you take on: the role sits at the intersection of three active charters, and you can move laterally across the full product-knowledge arc, from how selection enters the catalog to how it powers discovery, personalization, and fulfillment.

About the team
Our team owns the structured product knowledge that Shopping CX, Listing Ingestion, and Fulfillment Systems all depend on. While most product teams own a single surface, we operate upstream of nearly everything a customer sees — giving us horizontal leverage across the Stores business. The ontology is also the connective tissue for two major strategic investments: AI-powered shopping experiences and scaling how new selection is listed and ingested into the catalog. . We pair deep ontology, taxonomy, and schema expertise with broad cross-organizational product strategy, and we are looking for someone who can think like a platform provider and a customer-experience owner at the same time.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- Experience owning/driving roadmap strategy and definition
- Experience with feature delivery and tradeoffs of a product
- Experience technical product management

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working directly with Engineers on product enhancements
- Experience in project management methodologies, business analysis, or process improvement

title: Senior Technical Infrastructure Program Manager, QC Pre-Construction, North America Quick Commerce
descriptionHtml:
The Quick Commerce (QC) Pre-Construction team is looking for a Technical Infrastructure Program Manager III (TIPM III) to own the pre-construction strategy, technical design standards, site feasibility evaluation, and international design benchmarking for QC’s rapidly scaling North America network.

QC deploys multiple physical infrastructure formats, including Stand Alone and Co-Located sites, where pre-construction requirements vary by site type, existing building conditions, infrastructure capacity, permitting jurisdiction, and deployment scenario.
This role operates at the intersection of technical design and site readiness, defining how prospective QC sites are evaluated for infrastructure feasibility, how design packages produced by Architects of Record (AORs) and Engineers of Record (EORs) are reviewed for constructability and specification compliance, and how international quick commerce design approaches are benchmarked and adapted to improve QC’s North America standards.

The TIPM III will develop and maintain site evaluation criteria, technical design review standards, AOR/EOR performance frameworks, cost estimating methodologies, permitting strategies, and change-management mechanisms that govern QC pre-construction delivery. You will use technical domain knowledge to assess site feasibility, evaluate AOR/EOR design deliverables, identify design and permitting risks, challenge cost and schedule assumptions, benchmark technical solutions against international quick commerce operators, and provide feedback to Design Engineering, Real Estate, and Construction teams for specification and process improvement.

This role goes beyond reviewing a completed design package. You will define and continuously improve the pre-construction process itself into scalable standards that improve speed, design quality, cost predictability, and constructability across the QC portfolio.

Key job responsibilities
• Own and continuously improve QC pre-construction technical design and site evaluation standards across formats.
• Develop site feasibility criteria, technical design review checklists, cost estimating frameworks, and due diligence standards.
• Define new pre-construction processes where established evaluation methods, design review workflows, or permitting strategies do not yet exist.
• Evaluate prospective sites for infrastructure capacity, existing building conditions, constructability, permitting complexity, cost, and operational requirements to inform site selection decisions.
• Lead technical review of AOR and EOR design deliverables, evaluating design packages for constructability, specification compliance, infrastructure integration risks, code compliance, and alignment with QC deployment standards before construction handoff.
• Benchmark QC technical design standards against international quick commerce operators, identifying design innovations, infrastructure approaches, and deployment methodologies that can be adapted to improve QC’s North America standards.
• Partner with Design Engineering, Construction, Real Estate, SUEX, WHS, Finance, Operations, and external AOR/EOR partners to resolve complex pre-construction issues and align site evaluation criteria.
• Root-cause recurring pre-construction issues and translate findings into upstream improvements to site selection criteria, design specifications, AOR/EOR scopes, cost models, and permitting processes.
• Establish change-management mechanisms ensuring design learnings, cost data, jurisdictional findings, and international benchmarking insights are consistently incorporated into future site evaluations and design standards.
• Serve as the technical escalation point for complex pre-construction issues, determining whether gaps stem from site conditions, AOR/EOR design quality, cost assumptions, permitting, or evaluation methodology.

A day in the life
You start by reviewing a batch of prospective sites, assessing infrastructure capacity, existing building conditions, permitting jurisdiction complexity, and technical constraints to inform site selection and determine fit for QC deployment. Mid-morning, you lead a design review session on an AOR’s 90% construction document set, flagging a refrigeration layout concern and a fire protection code question that need resolution before permit submission. After lunch, compare QC’s cold-chain infrastructure approach against a leading international quick commerce operator’s design, identifying an equipment standardization opportunity worth exploring. You then join a call with a municipality and EDP partners to resolve an open plan review comment that is holding up a permit timeline. Before end of day, you document lessons from a recently permitted site and update the EOR scope of work template so the next design cycle captures requirements that were missed in this round. Your work turns site evaluation, design review, and international benchmarking learnings into repeatable improvements for future QC deployments.

About the team
The QC Pre-Construction team evaluates and prepares multiple site formats across varying building conditions, jurisdictions, and infrastructure configurations supporting Amazon’s Quick Commerce across North America. TIPMs work alongside Pre-Construction Managers, Construction, Design Engineering, Real Estate, SUEX, WHS, Finance, Operations, EDP, and external AOR/EOR partners to develop scalable pre-construction solutions. While Pre-Construction Managers lead day-to-day site evaluation and project setup activities, TIPMs define and improve the technical standards that guide how sites are assessed and how design partners deliver.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Architecture, Structural, Civil, Mechanical or Electrical Engineering
- 4+ years of construction or project management, or 10+ years of relevant discipline work experience
- Experience evaluating prospective sites or facilities for technical feasibility, infrastructure capacity, constructability, and deployment fit.
- Experience reviewing architectural and engineering design deliverables for constructability, code compliance, specification alignment, and infrastructure integration.
- Experience managing AOR, EOR, or A&E consultant relationships, including scopes of work, design deliverable reviews, performance management, and technical issue resolution.
- Experience developing or implementing pre-construction standards, site evaluation criteria, design review processes, or technical specifications.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience reading, interpreting, and creating construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents
- Experience delivering results for large, cross-functional initiatives/projects, or experience applying key financial performance indicators (KPIs) to analyses
- PE, RA, CCM, CPE, PMP, or similar technical/professional certification.
- Experience developing new infrastructure deployment processes or technical standards where established solutions did not previously exist.
- Experience leveraging data and technology to identify systemic infrastructure issues and drive process improvement across a portfolio.

descriptionHtml:
Vous aimez résoudre des problèmes concrets, mettre la main à la pâte et assurer le bon fonctionnement d'équipements essentiels ? Rejoignez l'équipe AWS chargée de maintenir des installations critiques, fiables et sécuritaires, 24/7.

En tant que Technicien en maintenance d’équipements électriques ou mécaniques, Installations critiques, électro mécanique, instrumentation vous réaliserez l'entretien préventif, le dépannage et l'amélioration continue d'équipements électriques et mécaniques. Votre travail contribuera directement à la fiabilité des services utilisés par des millions de clients AWS à travers le monde.

Ce poste s'adresse aux personnes ayant une expérience en électricité, électro mécanique, en mécanique, bâtiments, en maintenance industrielle, CVAC, énergie, manufacture ou services publics.

Si vous souhaitez évoluer dans un environnement technique stimulant, nous vous invitons à postuler.

**************************************

Do you enjoy solving real-world problems, working hands-on, and keeping essential equipment running? Join the AWS team responsible for maintaining critical facilities that are reliable and safe in our data centers 24/7.

As an Electrical or Mechanical Equipment Maintenance Technician, Electro Mechanic, Instrumentation Technician, or critical building mechanics Technician, you will perform preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement on electrical and mechanical equipment. Your work will directly contribute to the reliability of services used by millions of AWS customers worldwide.

This role is ideal for individuals with experience in electrical or mechanical fields, buildings,mechanical systems, industrial maintenance, HVAC, energy, manufacturing, or utilities. If you want to grow in a stimulating technical environment, we encourage you to apply.

About the team
À propos d'AWS
Expériences diversifiées
AWS valorise les expériences diversifiées. Même si vous ne répondez pas à toutes les qualifications et compétences énumérées dans la description de poste, nous encourageons les candidats à postuler. Pourquoi AWS ?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) est la plateforme infonuagique la plus complète et la plus largement adoptée au monde. Nous avons été les pionniers de l'infonuagique et n'avons jamais cessé d'innover - c'est pourquoi les clients, des entreprises en démarrage les plus réussies aux entreprises du classement Fortune 500, font confiance à notre solide gamme de produits et de services pour alimenter leurs activités.

Mentorat et croissance de carrière
nous montons constamment la barre de notre performance dans notre quête pour devenir le meilleur employeur au monde. Équilibre travail-vie personnelle
nous valorisons l'harmonie entre le travail et la vie personnelle. Le succès au travail ne doit jamais se faire au détriment des sacrifices à la maison, c'est pourquoi des horaires de travail flexibles et des arrangements font partie intégrante de notre culture. Lorsque nous nous sentons soutenus au travail et à la maison, il n'y a rien que nous ne puissions accomplir dans le nuage.

//

we’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Sr. Partner Marketing Manager, Global ISV Partner Marketing
descriptionHtml:
This highly visible role will own the Global Partner Marketing Strategy for a dedicated cohort of AWS Software & Technology partners, serving as the primary marketing owner of the partner relationship. The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of B2B and partner/alliance marketing, coupled with hands-on experience owning joint marketing plans, managing partner marketing budgets, and building executive-level partner relationships. You will be the subject matter expert on your cohort — accountable for the global co-marketing initiatives with and through those partners across sales segments and geographies.
The role will build and own a joint marketing plan with each partner in the cohort, aligning partner and AWS priorities into a single global co-marketing strategy and plan that drives pipeline and revenue. You will manage the global marketing budget for your cohort partner(s) — including MDF (Market Development Funds) — allocating investment across geographies and activities to maximize pipeline return, and holding partners accountable to agreed goals. You will set the strategy centrally and steer the Geo partner marketing teams to execute regionally, ensuring local activation ladders up to the global plan.
This role requires a proven leader with the demonstrated ability to think strategically and develop compelling joint value propositions and messaging with technology partners. Working closely with partners, partner management, sales, and marketing teams, you will define the joint value narrative — identifying the priority use-cases, customer personas, and industry verticals — and ensure that value prop is consistently carried into every co-marketing motion across the cohort.
The ideal candidate will be a strong relationship manager with analytic, data-driven judgment and a proven track record of building partner marketing strategies that drive pipeline and revenue. Critically, you will lead a v-team of Geo partner marketers — in addition to influencing key stakeholders across product, field, sales, and brand — coordinating them toward your cohort's marketing goals without direct authority. The ability to communicate and influence across both technical and non-technical audiences is essential. You should be organized, comfortable with ambiguity and rapidly changing priorities, and able to manage multiple partner relationships at once. A solid understanding of the cloud landscape and software providers is critical to this role.
At AWS we prize innovation, agility and a builder mentality. The organization is purposefully flat to enable fast decision-making and we are empowered to resolve issues, deliver new ideas and optimize existing ones that serve our customers. This is an individual contributor role that is both strategic and tactical: you will own the strategy, the joint plan, and the budget for your cohort, while orchestrating a v-team and partner stakeholders to execute — leading through influence as the composer who also knows the score.
This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in an incredibly fast-growing business where you will work with some of the leading technology providers. AWS gives customers secure, scalable, global cloud infrastructure while paying only for what they use. Scaling through partners is a key part of how we help customers move to cloud services that power strategic workloads. If you have an entrepreneurial spirit, a history of success owning partner marketing strategy and budgets, experience managing large ISV partner relationships, and love helping partners reach their full potential, this position might be just for you.


Key job responsibilities
Own the Global Partner Marketing Strategy for a dedicated cohort of AWS Software & Technology partners, serving as the primary marketing owner of each partner relationship across sales segments and geographies.
Build and own the joint marketing plan with each cohort partner, aligning partner and AWS priorities into a single global co-marketing agenda that drives pipeline and revenue.
Manage the global marketing budget, including MDF (Market Development Funds), for cohort partner(s): allocating investment across geographies and activities to maximize pipeline return and holding partners accountable to agreed goals.
Develop joint value propositions and messaging with partners: defining the priority use-cases, customer personas, and industry verticals, and ensuring that value prop carries consistently into every co-marketing motion.
Lead a v-team of Geo partner marketers and influence key cross-functional stakeholders across product, field, sales, and brand, coordinating them toward the cohort's marketing goals without direct authority.
Steer regional execution and measure performance, ensuring local activation ladders up to the global plan and optimizing investment against pipeline and revenue goals.

Basic qualifications

- 6+ years of professional non-internship marketing experience
- 7+ years of developing and managing acquisition marketing or channel programs experience
- Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements
- Experience with Excel or Tableau (data manipulation, macros, charts and pivot tables)
- Experience building, executing and scaling cross-functional marketing programs
- Experience developing and executing campaigns across a multitude of timezones and languages

Preferred qualifications

- Experience driving direction and alignment with large cross-functional teams and agency partners
- Experience designing and executing joint marketing plans with strategic alliance partners with global footprint

descriptionHtml:
AWS Compliance & Security Assurance is looking for an experienced Governance Specialist to support our Global Product Compliance (GTPC) team business on a broad range of regulatory compliance matters. You will interact with AWS Security, Datacenter Engineering, AWS Services, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, Legal, Tax, and other internal businesses and external stakeholders to drive operation policies and controls that provides oversight of AWS's product compliance posture. AWS is at the forefront of providing a broad set of global cloud-based services including compute, storage, databases, networking, analytics, deep Machine learning, robotics, and enterprise applications, to help organizations move faster, lower IT costs, and scale.

This is a dynamic business within Amazon.com, and one of the world's fastest growing and evolving companies, with a team of exceptionally talented, bright and driven people. GTPC is responsible for ensuring that the infrastructure equipment necessary to support the AWS services are imported/exported in a compliant manner across the multiple countries where AWS operates and will expand.



Key job responsibilities
Design and implement governance controls, SOPs, and policy frameworks governing Regulatory Operations processes — regulatory research, intelligence management, agency engagement, change monitoring, records management, and compliance auditing — ensuring each control is traceable to a defined risk or compliance requirement.

Define and execute country-level and product-level regulatory research methodology across all target markets. Establish and maintain a regulatory intelligence database with intake workflows, data quality standards, and refresh cadences that embed intelligence into hardware program decision-making.

Design engagement protocols and stakeholder maps for managing government regulatory contacts and agency relationships across all operating jurisdictions. Build and operate the process for monitoring regulatory changes; develop impact assessment frameworks quantifying risk to market access and program timelines.

Design and enforce documentation and records retention controls satisfying post-deployment audit requirements. Execute ongoing compliance audits and post-shipment surveillance obligations; develop audit checklists, sampling methodologies, and reporting templates ensuring consistent execution across markets.

Leverage compliance data and regulatory intelligence to identify emerging risks, maintain readiness dashboards, and present risk insights supporting leadership decision-making.

This person reviews regulatory change alerts, updates the intelligence database, assesses compliance risks against active hardware programs, refines governance controls based on audit findings, coordinates with government agency contacts, and ensures documentation archives remain audit-ready — maintaining continuous regulatory readiness across all operating jurisdictions.

title: Mgr, Post Delivery Ops, PAC
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
The Power & Cooling (PAC) team is seeking a senior leader to build and run the Post-Delivery organization — one of the three pillars of PAC Supply Chain Operations — accountable for getting every piece of Long Lead Equipment (LLE) from delivery through successful, on-time Power Facilities Hand Off (PFHO) at the scale AWS now builds. This is a broad, high-visibility leadership role: you will stand up a brand-new organization, lead leaders, set multi-year strategy, and own the outcome that gates every data center going live. The successful candidate is an experienced people leader who can operate at the strategic level with executives and across functions, while building the team, the mechanisms, and the culture that make on-time PFHO repeatable.
As the leader of the Power and Cooling Post-Delivery organization, you will build and manage a team across multiple areas — across Inventory and Logistics, Field Service and Commissioning Support, the Critical Spare Parts program, and post-delivery Global Supply Managers (GSMs) — responsible for commissioning readiness and issue resolution across global operation. This organization owns the end-to-end (E2E) lifecycle of every piece of equipment from delivery through PFHO. Your primary responsibility is to drive successful, on-time PFHO on a global scale and to develop the leaders and the organization that deliver it — hiring and growing, setting a single strategy and quantifiable goals, and representing Post-Delivery to senior leadership and to partner organizations across Construction, Technical Infrastructure Program Managers (TIPMs), Design, Category Management, and suppliers.
This is a transformational, build-it mandate rather than a steady-state operations job. Today post-delivery work is scattered across functions as a part-time responsibility; you will consolidate it into one accountable organization, set its operating model, and raise its performance as AWS scales — exercising the judgment to decide where to invest, what to escalate, and how to influence the functions upstream and downstream of you.
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own projects through completion.


Key job responsibilities
• Lead and build the organization — Hire, develop, and lead a team. Set direction and quantifiable goals, build the bench and succession for a largely new team, and establish a single, teachable standard of execution in place of individual improvisation. Developing leaders and growing the organization is the central, not peripheral, part of this role.
• Own on-time PFHO as a single-threaded leader — Carry end-to-end accountability for commissioning outcomes from delivery through PFHO, and be the senior escalation point and first line of defense for post-delivery construction and commissioning issues across the global build.
• Set the strategy — Own a multi-year Post-Delivery strategy anchored on a Site × Equipment commissioning-readiness framework, deciding where to concentrate commissioning enablers (Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) support and retainers, equipment and inventory redundancy, third-party field service, critical spare parts, and selective direct hires) against site and equipment criticality, and refreshing that strategy as the build evolves.
• Represent Post-Delivery to senior leadership — Communicate strategy, risk, and trade-offs concisely to executives; secure investment and air cover for cross-organizational moves; and influence partner organizations across Construction, TIPMs, Design, Category Management, and suppliers through authority and credibility rather than direct control.
• Run the operating mechanisms — Install the operating rhythm, metrics, and risk-management mechanisms that make on-time PFHO repeatable: forward-looking readiness over point-of-failure firefighting, a dynamic risk register across sites and suppliers, and feedback loops that drive recurring problems to their source.
• Scale what works and return capacity to partners — Scale proven commissioning programs (a supplier-managed Critical Spare Parts crash-cart, a Commissioning Success Scorecard, and Field Service Resource heatmaps) across the full supply base, and consolidate commissioning-phase ownership so Delivery GSMs regain the capacity for the sourcing and negotiation work only they can do.
• Success in this role directly impacts AWS’s ability to deliver data centers on schedule, measured by on-time PFHO, the health and growth of the organization you build, and the maturity of the mechanisms that sustain performance as the business scales.


A day in the life
• Set direction for your leaders, coach team.
• Communicate ideas concisely to a wide variety of stakeholders, for purposes ranging from informative to securing investment and approvals from executives.
• Embody a true pioneering spirit, willing to “get your hands dirty” in a start-up environment while simultaneously developing the strategy, processes, automation, and people that deliver results.
• Weigh competing priorities across many sites and suppliers, exercising high judgment on where to invest, what to escalate, and how to influence partners upstream and downstream.
• Develop and train leaders and teams to improve skills and capabilities for sustainable and continuous improvement.


About the team
*Why AWS* Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
*Diverse Experiences* Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
*Work/Life Balance* We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.
*Inclusive Team Culture* Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon ( diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.
*Mentorship and Career Growth* We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Solution Architect, Vehicle Technology CoE
descriptionHtml:
AWS's Vehicle Technology Team is a global Center of Excellence covering AMER, EMEA and APJ. It helps automakers, Tier-1 suppliers and mobility companies build the next generation of vehicles on AWS. As a Senior Solutions Architect, you'll set the worldwide technical strategy for our three core areas: Software-Defined Vehicle (SDV), ADAS/Autonomous Driving, and E/E Architecture. You'll be the technical lead on pilot engagements with strategic customers. You'll also choose and build relationships with key technology partners, and turn new ideas into demos for the industry's biggest stages.

This role is for a hands-on technologist who can talk architecture with OEM engineering leaders in the morning and build a working prototype in the afternoon. You'll have real influence on how AWS shows up in the automotive industry.

Key job responsibilities
Technical strategy: Guide the worldwide technical strategy for Vehicle Technology across SDV, ADAS/AV and E/E Architecture, and turn industry trends into reference architectures and solution patterns.
Pilot customer engagements: Lead pilot engagements with strategic automotive customers from discovery through proof of concept, and help turn them into production pipeline.
Partner ecosystem: Choose and work closely with key automotive partners (silicon, simulation, middleware, toolchain and systems integrators) to build joint solutions.
Industry demos: Build demos for flagship events such as AWS re:Invent, CES and IAA Mobility, working with account solutions architects.
Ambassador programs: Represent AWS in strategic technology ambassador programs, such as with NVIDIA and OpenAI.
Thought leadership: Speak at conferences, write blogs and whitepapers, and give product teams feedback from the field.

A day in the life
No two days are the same. In the morning you might meet with the E/E architecture team at a European OEM to look at how a zonal compute design maps to a cloud-native development and validation toolchain. Around midday you could join a working session with a silicon or simulation partner to scope a joint reference architecture for virtual ECUs and large-scale ADAS simulation. In the afternoon you might get hands-on with a prototype for the next CES or IAA Mobility demo, working with an account solutions architect who has a customer ready to see it.


About the team
The Vehicle Technology Team is a global Center of Excellence in AWS Automotive, with members across AMER, EMEA and APJ. We help automakers, Tier-1 suppliers and mobility companies change how vehicles are designed, developed, validated and updated. Our focus areas are Software-Defined Vehicle, ADAS/Autonomous Driving and E/E Architecture.

Amazon Business takes the selection, pricing and convenience customers already know from Amazon and adds what large organisations need to buy at scale: multi-user accounts, spend controls and approval workflows, business-only pricing, invoicing and payment terms, and direct integration into the purchasing and finance systems they already run. It is used by some of the largest enterprises, universities, hospitals and government departments in the world.

The problem we solve is one almost every large organisation recognises but few have fixed. Indirect spend — IT peripherals, tools, cleaning and office supplies, safety equipment and hundreds of other low-value, high-frequency purchases — is usually spread across dozens of suppliers, approved by hand, and invisible until the end of the quarter.

Australia is an early market for Amazon Business, targeting Enterprise and Strategic customers. You will own a named set of customers: some already buying with us and ready to scale enterprise-wide, others we have never sold to at all. There is no finished playbook to inherit. You will decide how these accounts are approached, and your decisions will visibly shape how Amazon Business covers this market.

Key job responsibilities
- Own a named set of Enterprise and Strategic accounts — including the account plan, the priorities and the revenue goal. Meet or exceed targets for both winning new customers and growing existing ones.
- Own all facets of the relationship for large, complex organisations, from first contact through to enterprise-wide expansion.
- Own the pipeline — drive how outreach and engagement is run, keep Salesforce accurate, and represent your territory in weekly and monthly business reviews.
- Build relationships up to VP (Vice President) and SVP (Senior Vice President) level, including Chief Procurement Officers and Heads of Procurement, and across Finance, Operations, Supply Chain, IT and Facilities.
- Understand the customer's operational processes, workflows and enterprise systems well enough to design a solution that fits, then drive adoption of the capabilities that make buying stick.
- Lead complex negotiations to conclusion across multiple stakeholders and functions.
- Work with partner teams including professional services, integration specialists, marketing, retail/3P and customer services.
- Prepare strategic account plans and written narratives for internal executives and stakeholders.

A day in the life
No two days look the same. You might spend the morning with a customer's procurement leadership on their indirect spend, the afternoon with their IT or finance team on how Amazon Business connects to their purchasing system, and finish by writing the account plan that gets an internal decision made.

Your customers are Australian enterprises, universities, hospitals and government departments. Internally you will work with professional services, integration specialists, marketing, business development and customer service.

You will be trusted to run your territory like your own business, with a global team behind you when a deal needs it.

title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (Model Customization and Optimization)
locations: East Palo Alto, CA, United States
descriptionHtml:
As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer (Senior FDE) on the Custom Model and Optimization team, you are the technical lead embedded inside a strategic customer, accountable for building, optimizing, and running the custom generative AI models at the heart of their business. You set the technical direction for model customization and optimization engagements, deciding what to build, how to measure it, and how it reaches production. You combine the technical depth of an AWS senior engineer with the urgency of a startup builder, using your judgment and ownership to deliver measurable business outcomes in quality, latency, and cost.

Senior FDEs work on the hardest problems where models meet systems: building domain foundation models, post-training frontier-scale open-weight models with reinforcement learning, and migrating large training and inference workloads onto AWS Trainium. They take on problems where the business problem itself is ambiguous, define the approach, and break it into workstreams others can own. They make long-term architectural trade-offs, balance customer urgency against sustainable design, and are trusted by customer engineering leadership as a technical peer. They raise the bar for the team through design reviews, code reviews, mentorship, and hiring, and they shape how AWS builds.

Key job responsibilities
Lead the technical engagement: Embed with the customer as the technical lead for their model customization and optimization program, spanning multiple workstreams. Partner with customer engineering and product leadership to frame the business problem, define success metrics and the evaluation bar, and set technical roadmap that moves from proof of value to production. Communicate trade-offs, risks, and results clearly to executives and engineers alike. Requires up to 25% travel.

Define the customization strategy: Decide the right path to the customer's quality, latency, and cost targets — prompting, distillation, supervised fine-tuning, preference optimization, reinforcement learning (including RL with verifiable rewards and multi-turn agentic RL), continued pre-training, task-specific adapters, or building a domain foundation model. Own the data strategy, synthetic data generation, and evaluation methodology that make those decisions defensible, and drive them to production for patterns such as coding agents, vertical foundation models, and multi-adapter serving.

Architect training and inference systems at scale: Design distributed training and RL post-training systems for large dense and mixture-of-experts models using frameworks such as PyTorch FSDP2, Megatron-LM, Miles, and verl, and production inference architectures using engines such as SGLang and vLLM. Architect RL interaction harnesses using frameworks such as NeMo Gym and OpenEnv, defining how agent workflows, tools, environments, and reward functions connect to training and evaluation. Set parallelism, precision, and serving strategies that balance throughput, latency, memory, reliability, and cost per token, and ensure the designs hold up under production load.

Lead optimization on AWS AI chips: Lead migrations of training and inference workloads to AWS Trainium using the AWS Neuron SDK. Diagnose performance and accuracy-parity gaps against GPU baselines, direct kernel-level optimization where it matters, and work with AWS Neuron and service teams to close capability gaps. Turn benchmark evidence into recommendations that shape customer infrastructure and capacity decisions.

Lead, mentor, and raise the bar: Provide technical leadership to a team of FDEs and scientists on the engagement, breaking ambiguous problems into well-scoped workstreams and unblocking others. Mentor FDE IIs on model systems design and production ownership. Lead design reviews, provide high-judgment code review, and actively participate in hiring and interviewing.

Multiply impact across AWS: Identify patterns across engagements and turn them into reusable fine-tuning recipes, evaluation frameworks, benchmarking tools, and reference architectures adopted by other teams. Influence the roadmaps of AWS services, including Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and AWS Neuron, with field evidence. Identify and shape opportunities to expand model customization and optimization within your customer and across similar customers.

Oversee engagement execution: Own the delivery plan, set milestones, track progress against deadlines, and ensure the quality and completeness of all deliverables. Hold yourself and the team accountable for commitments made to the customer, escalate risks early, and adjust scope or resources when timelines are at risk.

About the team
Team

The Custom Models & Optimization team, part of the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering team, partners with enterprises, AI-native startups, and foundation model providers to build, customize, and optimize generative AI models at scale. Our work spans domain foundation models, post-training of open-weight models, and moving training and inference onto AWS Trainium. As embedded engineers within the AWS Forward Deployed Engineering motion, we bring deep model and optimization expertise to customers' most strategic AI workloads, and we turn what we learn into tooling and patterns that scale across AWS.

title: Engineering Operations Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.

NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.

Key job responsibilities
• Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
• Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
• Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
• Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
• Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
• Technical writing to support change management program
• Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
• On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
• Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12 hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
• Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
• Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
• Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
• Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
• Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
• Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
• Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
• Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
• Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.



A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

2+ years of data center engineering experience
Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings
Vocational/technical training or an associate degree or above, or 4+ years of military experience

title: Partner Solutions Architect, ASEAN APO Partner Solutions Architecture Team
descriptionHtml:
AWS is where innovation, risks, and ideas are celebrated. We are builders, we try new things, and imagine big dreams. It is still Day 1 for us, and we are looking for curious people to be part of our diverse teams of thinkers, testers, and doers. Come join us and work with the latest cloud technologies that enable our customers to adopt cloud-based solutions.

THE ROLE
You will collaborate with a diverse partner community—including distributors, traditional system integrators, born-in-cloud partners, and AI-native partners—alongside other AWS teams to build architectures, proof of concepts, and demonstrations of AWS services by working backwards from their customers' business needs to accelerate the adoption of appropriate AWS technology.
A key focus of this role is accelerating both migration and AI transformation through partners. You will drive large-scale migration initiatives while simultaneously building and scaling an Agentic Platform that empowers partners to deliver AI-driven, autonomous solutions to their customers. You will help shape and design partner solutions covering a spread of domains from migration of core applications and workloads to working with GenAI, Agentic AI, AI/ML, microservices, containers, app development, IoT, and more. Being able to continuously expand your technological knowledge—particularly in migration methodologies and emerging agentic and autonomous AI capabilities—and having an interest in designing industry-applicable architectures that demonstrate business value are essential for this role.
PARTNER COMMUNITY MANAGEMENT
You will be responsible for managing and scaling relationships across multiple partner types to accelerate both migration and AI adoption:
• Distributors: Enable and empower distribution partners to extend AWS reach, providing technical enablement for migration and AI services, go-to-market support, and architectural guidance that cascades through their partner networks
• Traditional System Integrators: Work with established SI partners to modernize their migration practices, integrate AWS services into their delivery models, and help them evolve their capabilities to include AI and agentic solutions alongside traditional migration offerings
• Born-in-Cloud Partners: Engage with cloud-native partners who have built their business models around cloud technologies, helping them scale their AWS migration practices and develop advanced capabilities in emerging AI technologies
• AI Partners: Collaborate with AI-native and specialized AI partners to co-innovate on industry solutions, integrate their technologies with AWS services, and accelerate customer adoption of intelligent, autonomous systems that complement migration journeys
MIGRATION ACCELERATION
You will drive migration velocity and scale through your partner community by:
• Enabling partners to execute large-scale migration programs using AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP) and other migration frameworks
• Building partner capabilities in migration assessment, planning, and execution methodologies
• Developing migration-specific reference architectures, tools, and accelerators for partners
• Coaching partners on migration best practices, including the 7Rs (Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, etc.)
• Helping partners integrate AI/ML capabilities into migration workflows to optimize and accelerate customer migrations
• Driving partner-attached migration ARR and ensuring successful migration outcomes
AGENTIC PLATFORM DEVELOPMENT
A critical component of your role is building up an Agentic Platform for partners that enables them to:
• Develop, deploy, and scale autonomous AI agents that can reason, plan, and execute complex tasks
• Integrate agentic capabilities into their existing migration and modernization solutions
• Leverage AWS AI/ML services to create intelligent, self-improving systems that enhance migration and post-migration optimization
• Build partner competencies and certifications around agentic AI technologies
• Create reusable frameworks, reference architectures, and accelerators for agentic solutions that complement migration journeys
TRUSTED TECHNICAL ADVISOR
As a trusted technical advisor, you'll use your interpersonal skills to influence a variety of stakeholders—from technical teams to executives—across your partner community. You'll help ensure their short-term technology decisions around migration and AI are aligned with their long-term strategic goals. Helping partners work with customers to accelerate adoption of AWS migration services and AI capabilities will be part of your day-to-day activities.
COMMUNITY EVANGELIST & THOUGHT LEADER
You'll also act as an evangelist in the wider community. This includes taking part in educating, sharing best practices, presenting at events, writing whitepapers, blogs, and running workshops focused on partner enablement, migration acceleration, agentic AI, and emerging technologies. You won't just want to be part of an industry movement; you'll want to be leading it.
BUILDER & PRODUCT INFLUENCER
As a Builder, you'll also have the chance to shape the direction of our products and services. This is through gathering feedback from partners and their customers whilst collaborating with our engineering and service teams to influence the roadmap of AWS's migration tools, agentic capabilities, and AI services.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
- 3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
- 3+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of experience in infrastructure architecture, database architecture, networking and application development, including designing and delivering complex, large-scale enterprise solutions
- Knowledge of enterprise application platforms, middleware, containers, serverless and distributed systems, and their architecture, scalability, security and resiliency needs
- Hands-on experience with modern software development practices, including CI/CD, DevOps, Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, AWS CDK) and API-driven, microservices-based architectures
- Experience working with end-user or developer communities, including building technical content, running workshops and enabling teams to adopt new technologies
- Experience managing relationships with enterprise customers and technology partners (ISVs, Systems Integrators, Consulting Partners) to drive solution design and adoption
- Experience modernizing and migrating legacy or monolithic applications and infrastructure to cloud-native architectures
- Experience designing and building solutions in domains such as Generative / Agentic AI, data & analytics, and event-driven integration
- Industry certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional, AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional or equivalent

title: Regional Project Design Controls Engineer - APJC, Fleet Remediation Engineering
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and their servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

We have an immediate opening for a Project Design Controls Engineer in Sydney. If you meet these qualifications, exude passion, and enjoy the challenge of innovative projects at hyper-scale, this job is for you!

As a Controls Engineer within the Fleet Remediation Engineering (FRE) team, you will lead the design, specification, and implementation of Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) controls solutions for data center retrofit projects. You will bridge the gap between mechanical/electrical retrofit design and controls integration, ensuring that upgraded systems are properly monitored, controlled, and optimized across our existing fleet. This role combines deep controls engineering expertise with the fleet remediation mission of evolving our data centers to meet ever-changing customer needs at hyper-scale. You will use your Controls expertise to:

• Own the design for existing data center upgrades and design-solutions which add data center infrastructure, capacity, improve availability, and/or increase sustainability.
• Develop and maintain deep expertise in building operations, mechanical plant strategies, BMS/EPMS programming concepts, control diagrams, industrial HVAC systems, electrical lineups, one-line diagrams, and complex environmental concepts.
• Perform design and equipment submittal review for Data Centers in your region.
• Interface with internal and external data center design engineering team, server hardware team, environmental health and safety team, field engineering, and controls engineering to promote standards that maintain consistency and reliability in services delivered.
• Work on concurrent projects, sometimes in multiple geographical regions.
• Act as a technical subject matter expert for your given discipline during new remediation projects.
• Support construction, commissioning, operations, and turnover.

Key job responsibilities
Amazon's vision is to be the world's most customer-centric company, and this role is key to that vision. As a Fleet Remediation Project Design Controls Engineer, you will be leading projects to fit out our data centers to meet ever-evolving customer needs as we continue expanding our fleet to hyper-scale. As an ideal candidate you:
• Lead controls design and integration for mechanical and electrical retrofit projects across the existing data center fleet, ensuring BMS and EPMS systems are properly specified, programmed, and commissioned.
• Develop and maintain controls design standards, specifications, and scope of work (SOW) documents specific to fleet remediation retrofit projects, aligning with global design standards.
• Collaborate with FRE mechanical engineers, electrical engineers, construction teams, commissioning, and operations stakeholders to deliver integrated controls solutions that support retrofit objectives.
• Serve as the central technical authority for BMS/EPMS controls within FRE, managing and prioritizing controls scope across retrofit projects, legacy site enhancements, and capacity recovery initiatives.
• Perform controls design reviews on retrofit packages, identifying risks, gaps, and opportunities for optimization in monitoring and automation strategies.
• Coordinate with controls vendors and programmers on bid reviews, RFI support, controller drawings, MOPs, and code reviews, ensuring deliverables meet FRE standards.
• Develop and review control sequences of operation, control diagrams, point lists, and network architecture for retrofit applications including HVAC upgrades, power distribution modifications, and liquid cooling integrations.
• Interact with AWS cloud services and data analytics platforms to support data reporting, energy optimization, and operational intelligence initiatives.
• Anticipate roadblocks and risks in controls integration, providing escalation management and proactive solutions to maintain project timelines.
• Travel domestically and internationally as needed to support retrofit project initiatives, site surveys, and commissioning activities.
• Provide engineering judgment and design recommendations for controls scope despite uncertainty, particularly on legacy systems with limited documentation.

A day in the life
Each day you will interact with different teams responsible for all aspects of the data centers. You will prioritize your activities to support data center safety, remediation projects, capacity, and availability, focusing on the actions that are most impactful. You will have the opportunity to work on projects locally and globally.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic qualifications

- 6+ years of industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities experience
- 2+ years of relevant discipline work, or 2+ years of data center or mission critical facilities (example: hospital, military facility, public safety facility, etc.) experience
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related fields
- Ability to travel domestically and internationally up to 25% of the role.

Preferred qualifications

- Professional Engineer License
- Experience with EPMS/SCADA/BMS Controls system software or hardware
- 7+ years of industrial controls and automation experience
- Knowledge of Modbus, BACnet, and other industrial communication protocols.
- Experience with data center redundancy concepts, mechanical failure strategies, and failure mode analysis
