As a Software Development Engineer on this team, you will design and build the systems that customers rely on to provision, authenticate, and manage their IoT fleets — from a single prototype to billions of devices in production. You'll work on challenges spanning distributed systems, security, identity management, and scalable metadata storage and retrieval, directly shaping the experience for some of the world's largest IoT deployments.

This is a high-impact role where your work will be felt across the entire AWS IoT platform and by customers spanning multiple industries — from smart home and automotive to broadcasting and industrial automation. If you're excited about building foundational infrastructure that operates at Internet of Things scale and solving hard problems in device identity and registry, we'd love to hear from you.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and maintain core services that power device identity and state management for AWS IoT Core, serving billions of devices worldwide
- Build and operate highly available, low-latency distributed systems that handle device provisioning, authentication, metadata and state management
- Own the full software development lifecycle — from requirements gathering and design through implementation, testing, deployment, and production operations
- Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate in code reviews to maintain a high engineering bar across the team

- Mentor and support fellow engineers through knowledge sharing, design discussions, and constructive code reviews
- Identify opportunities to improve engineering processes, developer productivity, and system efficiency, including leveraging AI to automate workflows, enhance testing, and accelerate delivery

A day in the life
You'll spend focused time writing code — building new APIs, tuning system performance to reduce latency at billion-device scale, or improving provisioning workflows. You'll collaborate with teammates through design reviews and code reviews, and partner with other IoT Core teams on cross-cutting features. Some days you'll dig into customer escalations, tracing issues through logs and metrics. Other days you'll experiment with AI tools to improve engineering processes. No two days are the same, but every day you're building the foundation that enables billions of devices to connect to AWS IoT.

The Identity and Registry team owns the foundational services at the core of AWS IoT — device identity, registry, shadow, and provisioning. We build and operate systems that enable billions of devices to securely connect, be managed, and interact with the cloud. Our team values operational excellence, customer obsession, and a strong ownership culture where every engineer has a direct impact. We're a collaborative group that enjoys tackling hard distributed systems problems together, and we're committed to growing each other through mentorship and open technical debate. title: Software Development Engineer - AgentCore, AWS Agentic AI
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is building the foundational services developers use to create, deploy, and operate production-ready AI agents at scale. AgentCore Harness, launched at AWS Summit New York in June 2026, provides a managed agent loop that enables customers to define an agent through configuration rather than build and operate orchestration infrastructure themselves.

Customers specify their model, instructions, tools, skills, memory, and execution limits. AgentCore Harness manages the agent loop, secure execution environment, session isolation, identity, networking, observability, and deployment lifecycle. This allows developers to move quickly from an idea to a production agent while retaining the flexibility to integrate custom tools, models, and environments.

As a Software Development Engineer, you will design, implement, test, deploy, and operate core components across the Harness control plane and data plane. You will solve challenging distributed systems problems involving agent execution, session state, tool orchestration, security, scalability, reliability, and low-latency streaming. You will own features throughout their lifecycle, contribute to technical designs, and deliver high-quality solutions for customers.

Harness sits at the intersection of AgentCore Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Observability, Browser, Code Interpreter, and Evaluations. You will collaborate with engineers across these services to integrate capabilities, improve cross-service APIs, and reduce friction throughout the agent development lifecycle.

A central part of this role is making sophisticated agent capabilities dramatically easier to use. You will work backward from customer needs to turn complex infrastructure and orchestration tasks into intuitive configuration, sensible defaults, reusable templates, and guided workflows. Your work will help customers move from an idea to a secure, observable, production-ready agent in minutes while preserving the flexibility advanced builders need for customization.

You will help develop capabilities that make agent development faster and more accessible. This may include simplifying how customers connect tools and memory, building richer agent templates and skills, automating permissions and resource wiring, shortening the build-test-deploy loop, and creating safer ways to evaluate and release changes.

This is an opportunity to join a newly launched service at an early stage, contribute to its architecture and customer experience, and deliver capabilities with broad industry impact. Machine learning experience is helpful but not required. We are looking for strong engineers with distributed systems experience, sound technical judgment, a commitment to operational excellence, and the ability to deliver in a fast-moving environment.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, test, deploy, and operate highly available control plane APIs, data plane services, and managed agent loops for production AI agents.
- Build secure, isolated execution capabilities spanning tool orchestration, memory, context management, streaming, identity, networking, observability, and failure handling.
- Develop integrations between Amazon Bedrock and third-party models, AgentCore services, MCP servers, AWS Step Functions, Strands Agents, and customer-defined environments.
- Implement versioning, endpoints, progressive deployment, rollback, evaluation, and optimization capabilities that help customers safely improve agent behavior.
- Analyze and improve latency, scalability, availability, resource efficiency, and cost controls across multi-tenant workloads.
- Simplify the developer journey across APIs, SDKs, CLI, console, infrastructure as code, and local workflows by building cohesive abstractions, templates, defaults, and automation.
- Work directly with customers and partner teams to identify and reduce friction, accelerate time to production, and balance approachable experiences with the flexibility advanced builders need.
- Contribute to architectural decisions within Harness and collaborate with teams across AgentCore. Help raise the engineering bar through design reviews, operational readiness, code reviews, knowledge sharing, and mentoring.

- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience

- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

title: EHS Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. As a Workplace Health & Safety Specialist (WHSS), you'll be at the forefront of transforming workplace safety culture at one of the world's most innovative companies. Your expertise and dedication will directly protect employees, ensuring they return home safely to their families every day. You'll facilitate new approaches to safety, combining technology with human-centered solutions to create an environment where safety and productivity thrive together. This isn't just about maintaining safety standards – it's about revolutionizing how we think about and implement workplace safety, making a lasting impact on our people and operations. As your building's designated safety champion, you'll have the unique opportunity to build relationships, influence positive change, and help write the next chapter in Amazon's commitment to becoming Earth's Safest Place to Work.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Program Excellence & Implementation - Drive comprehensive safety programs through data-driven strategies. Lead daily safety audits, incident investigations, and risk assessments while implementing innovative solutions to prevent injuries. Deliver engaging safety training that resonates with associates and promotes a proactive safety culture. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance workplace safety while maintaining operational efficiency.

Associate Advocacy & Cultural Leadership - Serve as a trusted safety advisor and advocate for associate wellbeing, building strong partnerships across all levels of the organization. Foster a culture where safety is everyone's priority through effective communication, coaching, and positive reinforcement. Develop strong relationships with frontline associates and leadership to drive behavioral changes and ensure safety best practices become natural habits. Transform safety data into compelling narratives that influence positive change and drive engagement in safety initiatives.

title: Onsite Medical Representative
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. descriptionHtml:
Do you want to help shape how the world's most advanced AI models get built? AWS is hiring a Principal Go-To-Market (GTM) Specialist for Amazon FSx for Lustre, the high-performance file system behind some of the most demanding compute workloads on the planet. FSx for Lustre is a core part of the AWS Generative AI strategy. It feeds data to accelerated compute at the speed needed for training, fine-tuning, and inference at scale.

In this role, you will work with frontier model providers, fast-growing AI startups, and global enterprises as they build and scale their AI and HPC infrastructure on AWS. You will set the worldwide GTM strategy for FSx for Lustre and create and run programs, initiatives, research, and enablement at scale for our WW sales, specialist, partner, and cross-functional teams. Your work will directly shape how customers choose AWS as the place to build, train, and deploy AI.

To succeed in this role, you need a proven track record of building and executing GTM and sales programs at scale with measurable results, along with a strong understanding of HPC and AI/ML infrastructure.

In this role, you will be accountable for:

- Setting the WW GTM strategy for FSx for Lustre. Define strategic program direction and oversee execution of insight-driven programs that grow FSx for Lustre adoption and AWS market share with frontier model builders, AI-native startups, and enterprise AI and HPC customers.
- Driving GenAI and HPC workload adoption. Use your business judgment to drive revenue, build sales plays, and find new markets and opportunities across model training, fine-tuning, inference, and traditional HPC workloads such as genomics, EDA, seismic processing, financial simulation, and autonomous vehicle development.
- Working directly with the most demanding customers. Engage with leading AI labs, model providers, and enterprises to understand their performance, scale, and data pipeline needs, and turn them into product feedback, customer wins, and repeatable patterns.
- Partnering across AWS. Work with Compute (accelerated instances and UltraClusters), Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, Amazon EKS, Amazon S3, the Startups and Generative AI teams, industry teams, and service teams to align on joint GTM motions and find the workloads that drive FSx for Lustre growth.
- Mapping technology to business outcomes. Help customers understand how high-performance storage speeds up time to train, improves accelerator utilization, and lowers the total cost of AI and HPC infrastructure.
- Building enablement and evangelizing the platform. - Use excellent written and verbal communication skills to build sales enablement tools, reference architectures, and customer-facing content. -- - Represent FSx for Lustre with customers, partners, analysts, at industry events, and as the primary Executive Briefing Center voice for high-performance storage.

- Advising with data. Act as a trusted business advisor. Dive deep into pipeline, consumption, and win/loss data, create high-impact programs, track progress, and adjust to hit goals.
- Leading virtual teams. Guide cross-functional teams across sales, solutions architecture, product, and marketing to drive adoption in priority GenAI and HPC workloads.
- Owning goals. Define, drive, measure, manage, and coach on workload-focused goals across the worldwide business.

The ideal candidate can drive engagements and influence decisions at the CxO and VP level, and can also speak credibly with ML researchers, infrastructure engineers, HPC architects, and platform teams. You know how to build and deliver compelling value propositions, and you can work across the business to set vision and objectives and build consensus. title: Product Manager III, SCOT-International-JP
descriptionHtml:
Are you passionate about building products that solve real customer problems at scale? Amazon is looking for a Product Manager III to define product vision, drive strategy, and deliver meaningful outcomes that improve the customer experience. In this role, you will own the full product lifecycle — from identifying opportunities and defining requirements through launch and continuous improvement. You will collaborate with engineering, design, science, and business teams to build products that delight customers while driving measurable business results. If you thrive in ambiguity, love working backward from customer needs, and want to shape products used by millions, this is the role for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and own product vision, strategy, and roadmap, making transparent tradeoffs to optimize the sequence of deliverables and timelines while aligning with long-term business goals.
- Drive cross-functional collaboration with engineering, design, science, marketing, and operations partners to deliver products from concept through launch and post-launch optimization.
- Analyze usage data, performance metrics, customer behavior, and market trends to inform decisions, define success criteria and KPIs, and prioritize roadmap investments that maximize customer and business impact.
- Engage directly with customers and leverage research, usability studies, and feedback channels to distinguish between surface-level requests and underlying problems, ensuring the product stays grounded in genuine customer understanding.
- Evaluate and integrate generative AI tools and capabilities where appropriate to accelerate development cycles, improve decision-making, and unlock new forms of product innovation.

A day in the life
You start your morning reviewing key product metrics and customer feedback to identify emerging patterns. By mid-morning, you are leading a roadmap review with your engineering and design partners, working through tradeoffs and aligning on priorities for the next sprint. After lunch, you might join a customer research session to observe how users interact with your product, then translate those insights into refined requirements. Later, you connect with cross-functional stakeholders to build alignment on an upcoming launch plan and ensure operational readiness.

At Amazon, you'll work alongside the latest AI and GenAI tools that are increasingly woven into how teams operate: from AI-powered capabilities that accelerate decision-making, to Generative AI that helps you focus on work that truly matters. You'll have opportunities and resources to develop AI fluency at your own pace, with continuous learning built into the culture.

About the team
Our team is focused on building products that create real value for customers and the broader Amazon ecosystem. title: Lead Embedded & Controls Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a Sr. Embedded & Digital Control Engineer to lead the DSP/FPGA control architecture and embedded implementation strategy for the SST, coordinating hierarchical control loops and HW/SW co-design.

As a Sr. Embedded & Digital Control Engineer you will define the DSP/FPGA hierarchical control architecture — fast inner loops through supervisory control — where the structure must be established, not inherited. You will own real-time implementation constraints across power, FPGA and embedded layers and integrate control onto the target platform at system scale. You will drive stability/transient/dynamic-load validation and fault-state integration, and mentor control and firmware engineers across the program.




Key job responsibilities
Control architecture:
- Define DSP/FPGA architecture for hierarchical converter control.
- Coordinate fast inner loops, supervisory control and system-level control functions.
- Define control interfaces to power stages, sensors, protection and communications.

HW/SW co-design:
- Coordinate power-electronics, FPGA and embedded-software interfaces.
- Ensure real-time implementation constraints are reflected in control architecture.
- Lead integration of control algorithms into the target hardware platform.

System validation:
- Support stability, transient-response and dynamic-load validation.
- Coordinate control tuning and troubleshooting with Power Electronics and Simulation.
- Support fault-state and protection integration.

SST System Alignment:
- Lead the system-aligned state machine and system behavior implementation, including OFF, Standby, Precharged, ON, Fault and Warning states.
- Coordinate VRT/FRT, MVAC load acceptance/rejection, ESS power sharing, LVDC regulation, redundancy and recovery behavior.
- Define telemetry and control interfaces required for Modbus TCP/IP and the broader data-center operational interface.

A day in the life
In this role, you'll focus on architecting the digital signal processing and FPGA control systems that manage power conversion and distribution across our data centers. You'll start your day reviewing control performance data and collaborating with power electronics and firmware teams to refine real-time implementations. You might spend time defining control interfaces between sensors, protection systems, and communications protocols, then shift to validating system behavior under dynamic load conditions.

You'll also mentor other control and firmware engineers, sharing your expertise in hierarchical control design and helping them navigate implementation challenges. Your work spans from theoretical control architecture decisions to hands-on troubleshooting of transient responses and fault-state behaviors on actual hardware platforms.

About the team
We are the team that keeps AWS infrastructure running reliably across the globe. title: Lead Mechanical Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking a Lead Mechanical Engineer to lead the mechanical architecture of the 5-10 MW SST, including enclosure/rack architecture, interfaces, IP protection, vibration and seismic qualification.

As a Lead Mechanical Engineer you will define enclosure/rack architecture, interfaces, IP rating and serviceability for the 5–10 MW system from an open requirement space. You will own structural, thermal, environmental (vibration/seismic) and manufacturability constraints at system scale, plus escalations. You will chair mechanical reviews, coordinate suppliers/manufacturing, mentor designers, and align interfaces with thermal, electrical and MV/HV.

Key job responsibilities
Mechanical architecture:
- Define the mechanical architecture for the 5–10 MW system and its major assemblies.
- Develop rack/enclosure concepts compatible with high-power electronics and liquid cooling.
- Define mechanical interfaces with power, PCB, magnetics, cooling and electrical integration.

Environmental requirements:
- Address IP-rating requirements.
- Define and assess vibration and seismic qualification requirements.
- Consider serviceability, accessibility and maintainability in the mechanical design.

Design leadership:
- Lead mechanical design reviews.
- Coordinate suppliers and manufacturing for prototype and production parts.
- Support mechanical qualification, prototype builds and system integration.

SST System Alignment"
- Design against the system specification environmental envelope where applicable: NEMA 3R outdoor rating, -30°C to 40°C operating range, C5 corrosion class, 95% RH non-condensing, ≤1000 m site elevation and defined transport/seismic loads.

title: Real-Time Embedded Firmware Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Web Services is seeking an Embedded Firmware Engineer, Real-Time to develop deterministic real-time firmware for SST power-conversion control, PWM generation, diagnostics and protection-related functions.

As an Embedded Firmware Engineer, Real-Time you will develop bare-metal/FreeRTOS C/C++ firmware for PWM and conversion control on DSP/FPGA, delivered independently. You will adhere to ISR timing budgets, fault-detection latency and safe-state transitions coordinated with functional-safety requirements. You will debug real-time interaction between firmware, FPGA, control and power stages and supports HIL and system validation.


About AIS
AWS Infrastructure Services (AIS) owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Key job responsibilities
Firmware development:
- Develop bare-metal and/or FreeRTOS firmware in C/C++.
- Implement real-time PWM and power-conversion control drivers on DSP/FPGA platforms.
- Implement deterministic interfaces to sensors, control algorithms and hardware protection.
Diagnostics & fault handling:
- Develop embedded diagnostics and monitoring functions.
- Implement fault detection and fault-state handling in coordination with functional-safety requirements.
- Support watchdog and system-health mechanisms where allocated to embedded software.
Integration & verification:
- Bring up firmware on prototype hardware.
- Debug real-time interactions between firmware, FPGA, control algorithms and power electronics.
- Support hardware-in-the-loop and system-level validation.
SST System Alignment:
- Implement deterministic state-machine, protection, overload, fault recovery and power-sharing functions required by the SST system behavior.
- Support fast response to LVDC disturbances and coordinated ESS behavior during MVAC ride-through events.

A day in the life
As an Embedded Firmware Engineer, Real-Time, you'll focus on developing robust firmware for power-conversion control systems using C/C++ on DSP and FPGA platforms. Your day might include writing and optimizing real-time PWM drivers, implementing fault-detection algorithms that meet strict timing requirements, or debugging complex interactions between firmware, hardware, and control systems. You'll collaborate with hardware engineers and control specialists to bring up new prototype systems, validate designs through hardware-in-the-loop testing, and ensure your code meets the deterministic timing budgets critical to system safety. You may also contribute to solving real-time challenges specific to power-sharing and system recovery during grid disturbances.

title: EHS Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. As a Workplace Health & Safety Specialist (WHSS), you'll be at the forefront of transforming workplace safety culture at one of the world's most innovative companies. Your expertise and dedication will directly protect employees, ensuring they return home safely to their families every day. You'll facilitate new approaches to safety, combining technology with human-centered solutions to create an environment where safety and productivity thrive together. This isn't just about maintaining safety standards – it's about revolutionizing how we think about and implement workplace safety, making a lasting impact on our people and operations. As your building's designated safety champion, you'll have the unique opportunity to build relationships, influence positive change, and help write the next chapter in Amazon's commitment to becoming Earth's Safest Place to Work.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Program Excellence & Implementation - Drive comprehensive safety programs through data-driven strategies. Lead daily safety audits, incident investigations, and risk assessments while implementing innovative solutions to prevent injuries. Deliver engaging safety training that resonates with associates and promotes a proactive safety culture. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance workplace safety while maintaining operational efficiency.

Associate Advocacy & Cultural Leadership - Serve as a trusted safety advisor and advocate for associate wellbeing, building strong partnerships across all levels of the organization. Foster a culture where safety is everyone's priority through effective communication, coaching, and positive reinforcement. Develop strong relationships with frontline associates and leadership to drive behavioral changes and ensure safety best practices become natural habits. Transform safety data into compelling narratives that influence positive change and drive engagement in safety initiatives.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Must be available to work flexible shifts including days, nights and/or weekends.

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent
- A minimum of 1 year in an Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) related field OR; A Bachelor’s degree in EHS-relevant background OR; 6 months experience performing in a safety-related role within Amazon
- Knowledge of OSHA regulations specifically 29 CFR 1910
- Experience using Microsoft Word and Excel in a professional capacity
- Experience maintaining confidentiality in matter involving security and/or personnel issues in the workplace

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or higher, preferably in a safety related field
- Strong communication, teamwork, analysis, judgment, and customer focus skills
- Experience leading and managing a team, ability to analyze accident data, new processes, and machinery for potential safety concerns, and conduct job hazard and job safety analyses

title: Device Specialist, Device Management Team (DMT)
descriptionHtml:
Do you love hands-on logistics and working with technology before it hits the shelves? Amazon's Device Management Team (DMT) is looking for a self-motivated Device Specialist to join our Seattle operations, the team that ensures every prototype, beta unit, and production device across Amazon's entire consumer hardware portfolio gets where it needs to go.

- You'll work directly with physical devices daily, packaging, scanning, distributing, and coordinating shipments across buildings and around the world
- You'll support programs like Echo, Kindle, Ring, Fire TV, Eero, and Kuiper from earliest prototypes through mass production
- You'll be part of a small, high-impact team where your work is visible to senior leadership and directly tied to product launch success
- You'll have real ownership, managing your domain end-to-end, solving problems proactively, and building processes that scale as device volume grows
We need someone who thrives in a fast-paced, physical environment, can adapt on the fly when priorities shift, and takes pride in being the person others count on. If you want a role where no two days look the same and the tech in your hands hasn't been announced yet, this is it.

Key job responsibilities
This role requires daily hands-on work with physical devices, packaging, scanning, labeling, and distributing units across multiple buildings on campus. You'll be on your feet, moving between sites to meet program teams, deliver devices, and coordinate pickups throughout the day.

Core responsibilities include:

- Device fulfillment: Process allocation requests, pick and pack devices, prepare shipments, and assemble controlled return kits to meet same-day or next-day deadlines
- Inventory management: Receive incoming devices, scan into tracking systems, audit stock levels, and flag discrepancies before they become problems
- Cross-site coordination: Deliver and collect devices across buildings, coordinating handoffs with program managers and lab teams on tight timelines
- Triage and adaptability: Respond to urgent requests, troubleshoot delivery exceptions, and reprioritize on the fly when launch schedules shift or volume spikes hit
- Process improvement: Identify bottlenecks in day-to-day operations and propose solutions — better labeling systems, smarter routing, streamlined handoff procedures
The ideal candidate is someone who can see around corners, anticipating what's needed before being asked, adapting to shifting priorities, and proactively solving problems rather than waiting for direction. Physical presence and reliability are non-negotiable; our customers depend on devices arriving on time, every time.

A day in the life
Your day starts at standup, syncing with the team on what's shipping, what's arriving, and what needs attention. From there, you're processing device allocation requests, coordinating shipments with program teams, and triaging customer inquiries through SIM tickets. You might prep controlled device return kits, troubleshoot a delivery exception, or update logistics dashboards to keep leadership informed. No two days look the same, volume spikes with product launches and beta builds keep things dynamic. You're equal parts problem-solver, logistics coordinator, and process builder, with real ownership over how Seattle operations run.

About the team

title: HR Specialist, People Foundations, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Have you ever wanted to be part of a team building industry-changing technology? At Leo, we are building a low Earth orbit satellite network that will deliver broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities. Come join one of Amazon's most ambitious bets, scaling fast toward commercial launch with a workforce that spans hourly 24/7 production operations and corporate teams.

We are seeking an HR Specialist to serve as the programmatic owner for building, shaping, and onboarding Leo onto the people systems and mechanisms that HRPs, managers, and employees rely on. This role exists to unlock HRPs and managers by making sure the platforms, content, and listening mechanisms that serve Leo actually fit Leo's workforce, not configurations built for other populations. This role is a rethink of how the work gets done. You will work AI-native from the start, using AI to drive a step change in your approach and maximize output across programs, not just to do the same work faster.

You will own the work end-to-end, turning business requirements into configured, working solutions and driving them through the central teams that own the platforms. That includes standing up mechanisms that give leaders a real-time read on workforce sentiment and culture risk, getting Leo-specific content and policy into the right places while removing what does not apply, and locking in the right survey questions and definitions for both the hourly and corporate populations.

This is a portfolio and influence role. You will operate as an independent strategic owner, not a conduit. You will set the prioritization criteria that determine which requirements get resourced, build the intake and road mapping mechanisms the function runs against, and secure Leo's position in central roadmaps. Leo is smaller by headcount but outsized in business criticality, so it does not always compete for roadmap space on size alone. Your job is to make sure both populations are reflected in the systems that serve them, so HRPs and managers are not left to absorb the gaps.

This role is net-new. You will stand up the inaugural charter, mechanisms, and standards based on customer needs rather than inheriting an established playbook. While Leo is the primary portfolio, this role reports to the Sr. HRP Manager for Leo, Entertainment, Ads/IMDb/Grand Challenge, and Devices & Services (LEAD) and is designed to extend this programmatic muscle across LEAD business lines where similar people-systems needs exist.

Key job responsibilities
- Own the People Systems and Mechanisms Portfolio End-to-End. Own the work to build, shape, and onboard Leo onto its people systems and mechanisms. Run intake, set the criteria that determine which requirements get dedicated resources, and make capacity tradeoffs across active workstreams so the highest-leverage needs land first. Partner with the Leo HRBP team on central efforts like compensation and time systems.
- Build and Onboard Listening and Sensing Mechanisms. Partner with central science teams to stand up the mechanisms that give leaders a real-time read on workforce sentiment and site-level culture risk. Configure them so the signal is accurate and leaders get a self-serve asset, not one that requires HRP interpretation.
- Build AI-Native Mechanisms. Build AI into the portfolio's core mechanisms rather than treating it as an add-on. Set the standard for how AI-enabled workflows scale this work across LEAD, keeping human judgment on the tradeoffs and decisions.
- Configure Content and Policy Across the Central Platforms. Get Leo-specific content and policy into the right places and remove what does not apply, so self-service actually fits the workforce and directly unlocks HRPs and managers.
- Ensure the Mixed Workforce Is Correctly Represented. Lock in the right survey question sets for both the hourly 24/7 and corporate populations, and codify durable definitions the HRP role runs against, including how proximity is defined and applied.
- Own Portfolio Health and Surface Systemic Risk Early. Build the metrics and status mechanisms that show whether requirements are landing as working solutions, not post-launch defects. Spot systemic vulnerabilities in the intake-to-delivery pipeline before they become compliance exposure or business disruption and drive them to resolution through the owner teams you influence but do not manage.
- Lead Change Management and Write the Strategic Narratives. Roll out delivered solutions with the business and the HRP team, build scalable mechanisms and standards for intake and change, author the PR/FAQs and MBR/QBR inputs that articulate decision points and tradeoffs, and own inputs into OP1 and OP2.
- Extend Programmatic Capabilities Across LEAD. Scale this work across the broader LEAD business lines where similar needs exist, rather than solving them one by one. That includes thinking through hourly-population needs across business lines together, or owning scoping and implementation for shared tool rollouts, so one build serves many.
- Contribute to Initiatives Beyond the Core Portfolio. Take on work that requires programmatic execution, including people-systems integration for acquisitions and preparation for new site buildouts. Sequence the mechanisms so they are operational before the complexity lands.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent in Business, Program Management, Human Resources, Employment Law, Computer Science, Finance, Computer Information Systems, Engineering, Operations Research or a related field
- 7+ years of HR, talent acquisition, management consulting, or project/program management experience
- Can meet export control requirements by being a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum
- Experience translating ambiguous, high-stakes business needs into structured requirements and action plans
- Experience in project or program management across cross-functional partners for business operations or process improvement
- Experience partnering with central or shared-service owner teams to deliver outcomes through influence rather than direct authority

Preferred qualifications

- Experience prioritizing competing demands, scoping large efforts, and negotiating timelines
- Direct experience building, configuring, or onboarding HR systems, content, or listening mechanisms (for example TimeHub, Connections, or policy and content platforms), or comparable HR-systems configuration environments
- Experience supporting a mixed hourly and corporate workforce, where populations have materially different system, policy, and listening needs

title: Digital Sovereignty Specialist Solutions Architect
descriptionHtml:
AWS is hiring a Digital Sovereignty Specialist Solutions Architect for Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Southern Europe. You will help customers and public sector organizations move workloads to AWS when sovereignty, security, and regulatory requirements decide what can run in the cloud.

Organizations in highly regulated industries and the public sector across Southern Europe are deciding now how to meet their sovereignty requirements. You will be their technical counterpart for the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and for the sovereignty controls available in AWS Regions. You will also build on the work AWS has done with national cybersecurity authorities in the region, such as secure configuration guidance and landing zone templates aligned with national security frameworks.

Specialist Solutions Architects are part of the AWS sales organization. They bring deep domain expertise to customers with complex problems and work closely with account teams, AWS Professional Services, and Partners to help customers get to production.

This role is based in Madrid, Lisbon, or Rome. Native or professional proficiency in Spanish and professional proficiency in English are required. Italian and Portuguese are highly valued.

Key job responsibilities
- Advise customers, partners, and public sector organizations in Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Southern Europe on running workloads with sovereignty requirements on the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and in AWS Regions
- Lead the technical response to RFIs and RFPs that include sovereignty, security, and compliance requirements
- Work with national cybersecurity authorities, together with AWS security assurance and public policy colleagues, on cloud security guidance, secure configuration guides, and landing zone templates
- Deliver briefings, workshops, and architecture reviews for customers and partners, and speak at industry events
- Bring customer requirements to AWS service teams and turn field experience into whitepapers, blogs, and reusable content

A day in the life
Most weeks combine customer and partner meetings, time for focused work, and collaboration with colleagues across EMEA. A typical week might include a working session with a bank's security leaders on their sovereignty requirements, a review of the technical answers in a public sector tender with the account team, and preparation for a workshop with a national cybersecurity authority. You also set aside time to write, whether that is a secure configuration guide, a blog post, or feedback to an AWS service team based on what you hear from customers.

About the team
The Sovereignty Technology team helps customers, partners, and public sector organizations across EMEA adopt AWS. We cover the AWS European Sovereign Cloud and sovereignty controls in AWS Regions, and we work with regulated enterprises, software vendors and system integrators building sovereign offerings, national regulators, and EU institutions. Team members are based in several European countries.

In this role you will build expertise in European security and sovereignty frameworks, work directly with AWS service teams on the features customers ask for, and represent AWS with regulators and at industry events. You will have access to mentorship, knowledge sharing, and other career resources to help you grow.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let it stop you from applying.

- 5+ years in a technical role involving cloud architecture, security, or infrastructure
- 2+ years architecting or operating solutions on AWS
- Experience with security, compliance, or regulatory requirements for cloud workloads (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, ENS, C5)
- Professional proficiency in Spanish and English

Preferred qualifications

- Experience working with end user or developer communities
- Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics or equivalent

title: Global Stock Plan Specialist, Employee Investment Services, BXT
descriptionHtml:
Amazon is seeking a Global Stock Plan Specialist to join our Global Financial & Workplace Benefits team in Seattle, WA. This hands-on individual contributor role collaborates extensively with internal stakeholders and external partners to support stock compliance activities, including the regulatory reporting requirements of Amazon's global stock plans and mobility taxation. Qualified candidates will have stock plan compliance or mobility taxation experience.

The ideal candidate is highly organized and analytical, works effectively with internal and external contacts, and has a proven ability to manage critical projects concurrently and through to successful completion. They enjoy the challenge of improving processes in a highly dynamic environment, and demonstrate critical thinking skills, a strong focus on attention to detail with sound judgement, excellent written and verbal communication skills, and a passion for customer service.

Key job responsibilities
**Compliance Reporting**
• Support global stock plan reporting and compliance-related activities.
• Support implementation of regulatory changes to ensure program design and administration is compliant globally.
• Partner with internal and external business partners to research, provide input, and recommend compliance initiatives and policies.
• Perform audits and compliance reviews, including developing reporting and processes to communicate methodology, results, and remediation plans.
• Maintain an inventory of country-specific reporting obligations and track regulatory changes that impact stock administration programs and policies.
• Support month-end data reconciliation and internal audit activity.

**Mobility Taxation**
• Provide support in managing mobility tax positions, tax policies, and business travel policies.
• Process Restricted Stock Unit (RSU) releases for mobile employees.
• Maintain Amazon's third-party vendor tax calculation engine, including coordinating system enhancements to ensure accurate tax calculations.
• Provide program management support to the team that manages set-up of mobile employee tax profiles within Amazon's equity management system.
• Develop and execute new processes, procedures, and practices to improve efficiency, accuracy, and timely processing of equity transactions for mobile employees.
• Provide guidance and consultation, assess risks, and resolve issues and escalations as appropriate for employees, managers, and HR globally.

A day in the life
As a Global Stock Plan Specialist, you'll focus on supporting our stock plan compliance and mobility taxation initiatives. Your day might include researching regulatory changes affecting our global programs, coordinating with external tax specialists to validate calculations, or developing new processes to improve how we handle equity transactions for mobile employees. You'll work closely with our Financial & Workplace Benefits team, connecting with colleagues across HR, Finance, and regional offices to solve compliance challenges and implement improvements. Beyond routine compliance activities, you'll take on special projects like designing new procedures, conducting audits, and presenting findings to leadership—all while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

About the team
We are a collaborative team dedicated to ensuring Amazon's equity and mobility programs operate smoothly across all regions while maintaining the highest compliance standards. title: Applied Scientist, AWS Agentic AI
descriptionHtml:
Great code assistants have to understand code the way an experienced engineer does, not as a wall of text but as a living structure of symbols, calls, types, and dependencies that span an entire repository. Most AI tools today flatten all of that into tokens and lose the structure that makes real software navigable. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is assembling an elite team of scientists and engineers to fix that, and we are hiring an Applied Scientist to build the intelligence layer that lets our AI development tools reason about code through its true structure. You will help create generative AI technologies, including Kiro IDE and CLI, that are transforming how software gets built.

You will design how we turn the many signals around code, from static analysis and symbol graphs to build systems and language servers, into a single unified representation our models can reason over. This is a build-oriented research role where the questions are still open: how to fuse heterogeneous code signals, how to represent a whole repository so a model can find and use the right context, and how to ground an assistant's reasoning in the structure of real software rather than text alone. Your work will reach millions of developers, and you will own this direction end to end, from framing the approach to shipping it in a product engineers rely on every day.

Key job responsibilities
- Design a unified representation of code that fuses static analysis, symbol and call graphs, type information, and build system context

- Build the methods and models that consume that representation to power code navigation, retrieval, and reasoning at repository scale

- Invent and implement state-of-the-art machine learning solutions that operate at unprecedented Amazon scale

- Deploy products that directly impact the daily workflows of millions of developers worldwide

- Publish and present your work at premier ML, NLP, and software engineering conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, ICSE, FSE)

- Accelerate innovation by working directly with customers to rapidly transition research breakthroughs into production systems

About the team

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Hybrid Work
We value innovation and recognize this sometimes requires uninterrupted time to focus on a build. We also value in-person collaboration and time spent face-to-face. Our team affords employees options to work in the office every day or in a flexible, hybrid work model near one of our U.S. Amazon offices.

title: Quality Assurance Engineer II, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to shape the quality of a product that connects customers to the internet across the globe? Amazon's Leo ecommerce team is looking for a Quality Assurance Engineer II to own the frontend quality of the Leo website — the destination where customers discover, purchase, and manage their internet service. In this role, you will build test strategies and Playwright automation for a product that is actively expanding into new countries, giving you the chance to define scalable testing practices from the ground up. You will work closely with product managers, UX designers, and software developers to catch issues early, surface missed use cases during grooming, and raise the quality bar so that every feature meets customer expectations before it ever reaches production.

This is an independent, self-directed role where you decide where your attention has the most impact.

About the team
The Leo ecommerce team builds and operates the website where customers learn about, purchase, and manage their Amazon internet service. As Leo expands into new countries, the team is investing in scalable processes and automation to keep pace with growth. You will join a collaborative group of developers, product managers, and UX designers who value clear communication and a shared commitment to getting the details right. This is a great opportunity to build expertise in commerce at scale, international expansion, and modern test automation in the age of AI.

title: Pre-Construction Manager, GES NA, Design and Construction
descriptionHtml:
As a Preconstruction Manager within Global Engineering Services (GES) North America (NA) Design & Construction (D&C), you are Amazon's owner's representative during the preconstruction phase — responsible for independently managing difficult, cross-functional industrial building projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution across your assigned region. Preconstruction services refers to the planning of a construction project before actual construction begins.

You will partner with internal and external stakeholders to ensure scope, budget, and schedule definition are established, including timely receipt of building and site permits. You are responsible as the project manager to lead planning, design, and preconstruction projects — including new built-to-suit industrial buildings, tenant improvements, extensions of existing facilities, and renovation projects — supporting Amazon's logistics network infrastructure.

You work independently within your assigned region, using your knowledge of construction and project management concepts to decide which actions to take to complete projects, and seeking guidance as needed on strategic components. You are tactical with some strategic components, utilizing well-defined processes and best practices to facilitate delivery of high-quality results. You make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources to keep projects on track.

Key competencies of this position include ensuring that contracted resources deliver work product in support of project durations, permitting, key performance indicators (KPIs), and quality documentation; managing project teams (developers, design engineers, professional consultants); influencing internal teams (Design Engineering, Amazon Robotics); contract management governance; conceptual estimating and budget oversight; and managing multiple large industrial projects in various locations simultaneously. Translating technical documents and information into clear, concise narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers is essential.

This opportunity combines construction engineering, planning, project management, real estate development, design validation, site visits, understanding of local building and fire code issues, utilities, sustainability, multi-disciplinary design management, and contract management. The Preconstruction Manager is responsible for the planning and design of scope, budget, and schedule prior to handing off to the Construction Manager — focusing on taking ownership to resolve upstream issues and supporting the construction team throughout the process.

This role requires 60% regional travel on a yearly basis. When not traveling, you must have availability to work from a corporate office. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of one of the corporate office locations listed. Relocation assistance may be provided.


Key job responsibilities
Safety & Compliance
- Supervise the implementation and management of Amazon's safety programs and standards across all internal and external project teams during the planning and preconstruction phases of a project
- Interface and coordinate with Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) to ensure regulatory compliance, smooth permitting execution, and timely approvals
- Review noise, traffic, and environmental studies; understand zoning, planning, fire code, and building code requirements for assigned projects

Preconstruction & Project Management
- Independently manage difficult, cross-functional industrial preconstruction projects from site selection through design completion, permitting, and contract execution
- Lead site selection and validation, scope development, and design management — coordinating with design teams to develop site plans and composite floor plans in compliance with Amazon's design standards and operational requirements
- Manage multiple concurrent large industrial projects across various locations simultaneously
- Keep scope under control and accelerate progress by driving crisp, timely decisions, identifying and clearing blockers, and escalating appropriately
- Identify and resolve upstream issues proactively to support a clean handoff to the Construction Manager; remain a key support resource for the construction team throughout the project lifecycle
- Assess project performance through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for safety, quality, cost, schedule, and sustainability
- Minimize disruptions and proactively mitigate risks; plan ahead to prevent problems before they happen

Budget, Schedule & Contract Management
- Develop and manage project budgets and costs; own comprehensive schedule management and cashflow forecasting across assigned preconstruction projects
- Perform conceptual estimating and pricing reviews for scope inclusions and exclusions; negotiate the cost of work with developers, general contractors, and design consultants
- Contribute to the selection of external vendor partners and manage vendor procurement; oversee professional service providers to ensure their skills and competencies meet project requirements
- Review and analyze design and construction contracts, related exhibits, and lease agreements; provide detailed analysis of technical matters and site-specific deal structures and terms
- Partner with the Transaction team and developers to optimize schedule and strategy for entitlements and long-lead procurement
- Identify and solve factors that may impede a successful permitted project handover to Amazon stakeholders; make trade-offs between time, quality, and resources

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
- Work with internal and external teams — including Real Estate, Design Engineering, Entitlements, Construction, Finance, Launch/Startup, architects, engineers, permitting agencies, developers, and landlords — to secure resources, scope infrastructure builds, set priorities and milestones, and drive delivery to meet deadlines
- Drive results through communicating, weighing risks, making decisions, leading, and influencing; competently represent project and technical information to diverse audiences
- Maintain good working relationships with stakeholders and vendors; lead constructive dialogue to resolve and prevent project issues
- Act as the primary escalation point for project team members; own and track issues to ensure they are addressed, documented, and resolved

Communication & Reporting
- Prepare and present project status and risk reports; provide clear, concise summaries for projects under your ownership to leadership and management teams
- Translate technical documents and information into end-to-end narratives with detailed risk analysis for leaders and customers
- Run preconstruction meetings effectively — putting the right people in the room, checking progress, and driving high-level alignment and consensus
- Communicate budgets, schedules, project status, and priorities clearly to internal teams and external partners; trusted to present decisions to leaders up to 2-3 tiers above level
- Utilize Amazon's information systems to record and update schedule, budget, and other key project developments
- Represent Amazon's interests in weekly Architect, Owner, and Contractor (AOC) meetings; provide input on root causes and corrective actions

Process Improvement & Innovation
- Optimize preconstruction processes and implement improvements in procedures and playbooks to improve project efficiency and delivery
- Look for opportunities to improve operational excellence and influence the team to determine where to iterate and make improvements
- Seek sustainable, environmentally responsible solutions throughout the preconstruction process in alignment with Amazon's building practices
- Adapt to constant change and innovation; find adaptable solutions for an evolving business

A day in the life
Each day, you represent GES NA Design & Construction as Amazon's owner during the preconstruction phase — navigating uncertainty, proactively unblocking project barriers, and influencing the best project decisions. You are tactical with some strategic components, working independently and interacting with leadership to resolve issues. Your day may include:
- Coordinating with architects, engineers, and design consultants on design document development, scope changes, and project status
- Reviewing site plans, composite floor plans, and design documents for compliance with Amazon's standards and operational requirements
- Negotiating contract terms with developers, contractors, and consultants while driving adherence to schedules and budgets
- Coordinating with AHJ on permitting status, zoning, fire code, and building code requirements
- Preparing and presenting project status and risk reports for leadership
- Partnering with Real Estate and Transaction teams on entitlement strategy and long-lead procurement
- Providing estimating support, interpreting drawings, contributing to budgets, and reviewing lease exhibits
- Updating Amazon's project management systems with current budget, schedule, and status information
- Supporting the Construction Manager on active construction projects with preconstruction expertise

About the team
At Amazon, the GES North America Design & Construction team is a diverse group of engineers, construction managers, and preconstruction professionals who deliver the physical infrastructure behind Amazon's logistics network. We are employee owners who take pride in delivering high-quality, innovative facilities — on time and on budget — for our internal customers and the communities we serve. We are committed to being Earth's best employer and to building a more sustainable future through every project we deliver.

- 5+ years of experience as an Architect, Engineer, Construction Manager, Development Manager, Owner's Project Management Representative, or in a related commercial development or construction discipline

- Position includes travel up to 60% (Nationwide). Travel involves air travel to regional airports and driving to site locations. A valid driver's license is required due to project assignments in areas with limited public transportation and rideshare options.

- Demonstrated success communicating project requirements to diverse audiences (e.g., senior management, peers, fire marshals, utility providers, public officials, vendors)

title: Principal Forward Deployed Engineer, AWS Forward Deployed Engineering
descriptionHtml:
A Principal Forward Deployed Engineer (Principal FDE) embeds across multiple strategic enterprise customers to define the technical strategy and engineering standards for AI-powered production systems at scale. Principal FDEs write production-grade software, set the technical direction for complex multi-workstream engagements, and create the reusable architectures, patterns, and engineering mechanisms that scale the entire FDE practice — combining the technical depth of an AWS Principal SDE with the strategic influence required to deliver transformational customer business outcomes.

Principal FDEs independently lead software delivery across an organization. They drive clarity where neither the business problem nor technology strategy is well defined. They solve problems with non-technical solutions such as process improvement, culture changes, or staffing and training. They set the standard for engineering excellence, handle escalations, and drive closure with peers, Directors, and stakeholders. They are force multipliers whose impact extends well beyond any single engagement.

This position requires that the candidate selected must be a US Citizen and currently possess and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
Define technical strategy across engagements.
- Set the technical direction for the most complex, highest-stakes customer AI programs. Be a key influencer for strategic decisions, bringing technology and industry context to business decisions. Make architecture decisions that span multiple workstreams, services, and organizational boundaries. Requires up to 25% travel.

Build production AI systems and reference architectures.
- Design and build the foundational architectures — multi-agent orchestration frameworks, enterprise-grade retrieval systems, decision intelligence platforms — that become the template for future engagements. Tackle intrinsically hard problems, acquiring expertise as needed. Solve problems that are significantly complex not only because of technical complexity. title: Software Development Engineer II, Selection Monitoring
descriptionHtml:
Help Amazon understand every brand in the world and make sure customers can find the brands they love in our store. As a Software Development Engineer on the Universal Brand Catalog (UBC) team, you'll design and own large-scale data systems, AI/ML-powered services, and self-serve tools that show brand recruitment teams which brands are missing from Amazon and where to act. This is a new space with key architecture decisions still on the table, so you'll have real influence over the technical direction from day one. You'll work across the full software development lifecycle, collaborate closely with applied scientists and product managers, and see your work translate directly into wider selection for Amazon customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and large-scale data pipelines (Spark on Amazon EMR) that process brand, product, and marketplace data across Amazon's global catalog.
- Own features end to end — requirements, design documents, implementation, testing, deployment, and operations — and lead design reviews where you make sound tradeoffs between accuracy, latency, cost, and scalability.
- Partner with applied scientists to put ML models into production, measure data quality through precision and recall metrics, and iterate on brand-matching and gap-detection signals.
- Turn ambiguous business problems into clear technical plans, break large projects into shippable deliverables, and build self-serve tools that let business teams slice brand and selection data by market, category, and competitive trends without engineering support.
- Mentor junior engineers and interns through code reviews, design guidance, and pairing, while driving operational improvements in monitoring, alarming, and on-call health.

A day in the life
You might start the day at stand-up, then review a design document for a new pipeline that scores brands across marketplaces. Later you could meet with a product manager and a scientist to figure out how to measure whether a brand gap signal can be trusted, then turn that into a data model and plan. In the afternoon you'll write code, review a teammate's pull request, and help a junior engineer debug a Spark job. Your internal stakeholders include category and vendor management teams who use your data to recruit brands, partner catalog teams, and science teams.

About the team
The UBC team builds the foundation for how Amazon understands brands: which brands exist, how they relate to each other, where they're sold, and where they're missing from our store. We own Brand Gaps (finding brands and selection absent from Amazon) and Brand Cohort Management (grouping and prioritizing brands so teams can focus on what matters most to customers). Engineers and applied scientists work side by side on problems like signal precision, cohort ranking, and entity matching. The space is new and growing, so you'll have real ownership, see the business impact of your work directly, and grow through mentorship, design reviews, and a sustainable on-call culture.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Electronics Engineer, RIVR
descriptionHtml:
RIVR, part of Amazon is a robotics team pioneering Physical AI through real-world deployment and doorstep deliveries. Founded in 2024 as an ETH Zurich spin-off, RIVR developed wheeled-legged robots designed to operate in complex, unstructured environments such as stairs, gates, doors, and uneven urban terrain. We believe that achieving general physical intelligence requires solving real customer problems in the real world, where robots can learn by gathering rich operational data at scale.

As a Junior Electronics Engineer, you will spearhead the design, development, and testing of our robots' custom electronics. Your expertise will encompass power electronics (motor control, power distribution), digital electronics (PCBA design, microprocessor) firmware and communication protocols, ensuring that our robots not only meet specific application requirements but are also scalable and cost-effective for mass production. We value candidates with a proven track record of transitioning projects from prototyping and proof-of-concepts to MVPs, full products, and ultimately, mass production. - Experience in PCB design and firmware development.

- Knowledgeable in control systems and in common electronics components and communication protocols utilized in robotics or related fields.
- Strong problem-solving skills, adept at debugging and optimizing hardware components.

title: ファシリティエンジニア - DCEO（データセンターエンジニアリング・オペレーションズ）
descriptionHtml:
AWS Infrastructure Services はすべての AWS グローバルインフラストラクチャの設計、計画、提供、運用を担当しています。私たちは、クラウドを稼働させ続ける人々です。すべての AWS データセンターとお客様がイノベーションに継続的にアクセスできるようにするすべてのサーバー、ストレージ、ネットワーク、電源、冷却設備をサポートしています。私たちはサプライチェーンに影響を与える数千もの要因を考慮しながら、最も困難な課題に取り組んでいます。そして私たちと共に支援したいと考える優秀な人材を探しています。

ソフトウェア、ハードウェア、ネットワークエンジニア、サプライチェーンスペシャリスト、セキュリティエキスパート、オペレーションマネージャー、その他の重要な役割を担う多様なチームに参加していただきます。AWS 全体の人々と協力して、お客様に最低コストで無限の容量を提供しながら、安全性とセキュリティの最高基準を提供できるよう支援していただきます。そして、大胆なアイデアを歓迎し、それを完成まで自分のものとして進める力を与える包括的な文化を体験していただけます。

Data Center Operationsチームは AWS のバックボーンであり、急速に成長する AWS ビジネスとお客様を 24 時間 365 日サポートしています。私たちは AWS の物理インフラストラクチャを維持し、安全性、セキュリティ、可用性、生産性、容量、効率性、コストの分野における運用パフォーマンスの基準を確保することに取り組んでいます。



Key job responsibilities
主な職務内容

Facility Engineer - Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) の役割は、大規模で高密度のデータセンターにおいて、施設（電気/機械システム、制御/消火システムなど）の展開、運用、保守、および関連プロジェクトの管理を担当します。
日常業務では、以下の業務に携わります:
• 建物システムの点検と監視、および施設の問題のトラブルシューティング
• 運用効率の改善とエネルギー削減
• ベンダーやパートナーとの定期メンテナンスと修理の計画と実施。これには、ブレーカー操作、機械/電気設備操作などの重要な施設運用が含まれます
• プロジェクトチームメンバーと協力してテストなどをサポート

勤務時間

12時間のシフト勤務 (うち2時間休憩)など、標準外の時間帯勤務が可能な方（4勤3休のシフトで働ける方。標準勤務時間は 8:00 ～ 20:00、20:00 ～ 8:00、または 9:00 ～ 21:00、21:00 ～ 9:00 です）



About the team
多様な経験

AWS は多様な経験を重視しています。職務内容に記載されているすべての資格やスキルを満たしていなくても、応募することをお勧めします。キャリアが始まったばかりの場合、従来の道を歩んでいない場合、または関連しない経験がある場合でも、応募をためらわないでください。

なぜ AWS なのか?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) は、世界で最も包括的で広く採用されているクラウドプラットフォームです。私たちはクラウドコンピューティングのパイオニアであり、イノベーションを止めることはありません。だからこそ、最も成功しているスタートアップから Global 500 企業まで、幅広いお客様が当社の堅牢な製品・サービスを信頼し、ビジネスを推進しています。

包括的なチーム文化

AWS では、学び、好奇心を持つことが私たちの本質です。従業員主導のアフィニティグループは、私たちが自分たちの違いを誇りに思える包括的な文化を育んでいます。Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) や AmazeCon (ジェンダーダイバーシティ) カンファレンスを含む継続的なイベントや学習体験は、私たちが独自性を受け入れることを決して止めないよう刺激を与えてくれます。

メンターシップとキャリア成長

私たちは、地球上で最高の雇用主になるために、継続的にパフォーマンスバーを引き上げています。だからこそ、ここには、より多角的な専門家に成長するのに役立つ、無限の知識共有、メンターシップ、その他のキャリア向上リソースがあります。

ワークライフバランス

私たちはワークライフハーモニーを重視しています。仕事での成功は、家庭での犠牲を伴うべきではありません。だからこそ、柔軟な勤務時間と勤務体制が私たちの文化の一部となっています。職場と家庭でサポートされていると感じるとき、クラウドで達成できないことは何もありません。

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of relevant work experience
- Work shifts longer than eight hours in duration
- ミッションクリティカルな設備の運用と保守に関する 2 年以上の関連実務経験（例: 24 時間稼働の工場、変電所、病院など）
- メンテナンス、変更管理、インシデント管理、ベンダー管理の経験または基本的な理解、およびポリシー、プロセス、手順を遵守して作業する方法
- 12時間のシフト勤務 (うち2時間休憩)など、標準外の時間帯勤務が可能な方（4勤3休のシフトで働ける方。標準勤務時間は 8:00 ～ 20:00、20:00 ～ 8:00、または 9:00 ～ 21:00、21:00 ～ 9:00 です）
- 補助機器を使用して18 kg程度の機器を安全に持ち上げて移動できること

Preferred qualifications

- データセンターに関連する資格（CDCP、CDCS、CDCE、ASHRAE など）、またはデータセンター管理のための資格（第二種または第三種電気主任技術者、エネルギー管理士、第 4 類危険物取扱者、冷凍機械責任者、第二種電気工事士）
- プロジェクト管理資格（PMP、Prince2、ITILv2、BICSI）
- 電気システムに関する高度な理解力（変電所の電源供給システム、変圧器、スイッチギア、VFI クラス UPS、DRUPS、PDU、ATS、STS、SLA または VRLA バッテリーおよび関連システム、ディーゼル/ガスタービン発電機に関連する燃料システム、サージ制御回路、アクティブ高調波フィルター、バッテリー監視システム、分岐回路監視システム、SCADA システム）
- 機械システムに関する高度な理解力（CRAC/CRAH、AHU、チラー、冷却塔、貯蔵タンク、熱交換器、配管システム、ポンプ、バルブ、ダクトシステム、ファン、ダンパー、火災検知・消火システム、排水システム、ビル監視システム、自動制御システム）

title: WHS Specialist - Health & Wellbeing
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon we believe that every day is still day one; a day to take a first step; a day to look forwards to new challenges; and today is that day for you. It’s your day to be part of something great; a day to make your ideas come to life; and your day to join a company that redefines itself every day. That’s the energy and passion behind Amazon.

We are currently looking to hire a Workplace Health, Safety and Wellness (WHSW) Specialist to join the team and play a critical role in supporting the WHS function. The successful candidate will be an experienced, innovative, hands-on and customer obsessed individual, passionate about WHS, injury prevention, effective management of, and engaged return to work processes. Be able to identify, coordinate and drive improvements in WHS whilst engaging Operational and other Support Function stakeholders. The candidate will be keen to grow their career with Amazon as we continue to expand in Australia, and globally.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the strategy and act as the technical subject matter expert for musculoskeletal injury prevention and health and wellbeing program design across Amazon Australia.
• Own the onsite and telehealth physiotherapy program end to end across fulfilment centres, sort centres and delivery stations, including the service delivery model, site coverage and rostering, vendor performance against service levels and clinical and utilisation KPIs, purchase order and invoice reconciliation, and contract variations and renewals in partnership with Procurement and Legal.
• Build and run the program's governance, including standard operating procedures, weekly KPI tracking, case follow-up and dashboards, and report performance to leadership through weekly, monthly and quarterly business reviews and Board updates.
• Support the WHS Manager to deliver health, safety and wellbeing performance against team and functional goals, programs and projects.
• Drive the development and implementation of occupational health, injury prevention, early intervention, injury management and return to work programs, scaling successful site pilots into network-wide standards.
• Partner with site WHS and operations teams to implement injury prevention and wellbeing programs, and provide specialist support on physical demands assessments, task analysis and ergonomic risk assessments.
• Participate in incident investigations for musculoskeletal and physical health injuries, identify root causes and recommend engineering and work design controls.
• Support the business to maintain compliance with Commonwealth and state WHS legislation, codes of practice and Amazon global standards.
• Keep WHS systems accurate and complete, with incident reports and supporting documentation, and compile metrics to support regular and ad hoc reporting.
• Build the business case for program investment through the annual planning and budget cycle, using injury, cost and utilization data.
• Participate in WHS audits and inspections as required, and train and coach site teams and vendor physiotherapists.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or higher in Health and/or Safety, psychology, behavioural health, public health, health science or a related field
- Minimum 3 years’ experience, ideally in an occupational setting
- Knowledge of Workplace/Occupational Health and Safety legislation

Preferred qualifications

- Experience managing external physiotherapy or allied health vendors delivering workplace injury prevention programs, including contract and budget oversight, performance tracking against clinical and utilisation KPIs
