title: Data Center Materials Associate, Corporate IT Logistics, Operations, IT, & Support Engineering
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon, we strive to be Earth's most customer-centric company where people can find and discover anything they want to buy online. We hire the world's brightest minds, offering them an environment in which they can relentlessly improve the customer experience. Innovation and creativity are built into the DNA of the company and are encouraged at all levels of employment. Every day we solve complex technical and business problems with ingenuity and simplicity. We're making history and the good news is we've only just begun.

Amazon's IT Logistics and Imaging Team (ITS-LIT) operates a warehouse-scale production floor that images, provisions, and manages the lifecycle of every corporate laptop and device deployed to Amazonians across the United States. Our team at SEA124 (Ouroboros) in Renton, WA processes thousands of devices weekly — supporting new hire onboarding, device refreshes, inventory management, reverse logistics, and data destruction.

We are seeking a Data Center Materials Associate to join our warehouse operations team. In this role, you will support daily inventory and logistics work — receiving and inducting IT assets, picking, packing, shipping, and processing returns. You'll follow standard procedures, work through assigned tasks as priorities shift during the day, and focus on accuracy and quality in every transaction. You'll also help keep IT areas clean, organized, and audit-ready.

This is a hands-on warehouse environment where your work directly supports Amazon's ability to deliver devices to employees on Day 1.

Our team approaches work as seeing no job as too small and no challenge as too big!

Key job responsibilities
- Support daily inventory operations, including receiving, induct, storage, picking, packing, and shipping of IT assets and peripherals
- Complete assigned tasks across queues and programs, following daily priorities set by the team
- Restock IT inventory locations, vending machines, and supply stores, and report low stock to your lead
- Process returned IT assets following compute reuse, reverse logistics, and disposal procedures
- Prepare IT assets for transportation in line with IT and InfoSec policies, including safe handling and destruction of IT media
- Assist with removal and recovery of IT assets from campus locations as required
- Prepare new hire equipment kits and support campus IT staff during new hire orientation
- Follow standard operating procedures and flag issues or errors to your lead
- Complete assigned work within SLA and record progress in ServiceNow
- Work with teams across the warehouse (IT Support, Returns, Stock Cart, Imaging) to keep orders moving

A day in the life
You arrive at our warehouse in Renton, WA and check the day's work: inbound shipments to receive, outbound orders to pick and pack, and returns to process. Your lead sets the day's priorities, and you move between tasks as they shift. Some days you're building new hire kits for Monday onboarding. Other days you're processing returned assets, restocking vending machines across campus, or helping with a bulk removal from a decommissioned floor. You follow standard procedures, flag issues to your lead, update ServiceNow, and make sure every asset is accounted for. Your accuracy helps make sure every Amazonian has the equipment they need on Day 1.

About the team
We're Amazon's primary imaging center for North America — a warehouse team that prepares and ships every corporate laptop before an employee's first day. We process thousands of devices weekly across multiple imaging lanes and shifts. You'll work alongside engineers, technicians, and operations specialists who build their own tools, write their own procedures, and own their programs end-to-end. Our culture is hands-on, direct, and team-first. We value people who take ownership, communicate clearly, and look for ways to improve how things work. Every day brings something different.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English, and have the ability to take direction in English
- Experience with Microsoft Office products and applications
- Work 40 hours/week, and overtime as required
- Work 10 hour shifts as needed
- Are 18 years of age or older
- Can lift and rack equipment up to 40 pounds

Preferred qualifications

- Can show strong verbal and written communication skills
- Experience maintaining inventory, including receiving, storage, and auditing
- Experience with a ticketing system such as ServiceNow
- Self-motivated and customer-focused
- Able to manage multiple requests at once and prioritize based on team objectives

title: Community Impact Excellence & Standards (Global Procurement Organization), Global Procurement Community Impact
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's Global Procurement Sustainability team and build the operating backbone of Community Impact — the strategy, standards, regulations, donations excellence and governance that turn procurement into lives improved impact for communities across 26 countries.

As the owner of Community Impact Excellence & Standards for Global Procurement Organization (GPO) Community Impact (CI), you'll bring strategy, policy, standards, regulatory alignment, compliance, execution excellence, and governance to the full Community Impact program, spanning all five pillars: Supplier for Good, Procurement for Good, Waste to Worth, Space for Good / Donation Hubs, and AI For Good with IDonate. You'll set the standards and standard operating procedures that make impact consistent and compliant everywhere, drive execution to ambitious donation targets (including $10M in procurement donations in 2027), and make Community Impact visible all the way up to senior leadership.

Drive excellence — raise execution quality and consistency of CI programs across 26 countries

Own regulations & compliance — ensure CI activity is compliant, regulation-aligned, and auditable

Lead donations execution — including the Waste to Worth standard operating procedure and the $10M 2027 procurement-donations target

Govern & report — embed CI performance into Monthly Business Review and Quarterly Business Review forums and leadership communications

Set the strategy — shape the multi-year strategy for Community Impact excellence and standards

Key job responsibilities
Strategy — Own and drive the multi-year strategy for Community Impact excellence and standards: define the vision, the roadmap to scale consistency and quality across all five pillars and 26 countries, and the long-term path to a world-class CI operating model.

Standards, Policy & Process — Define and own the GPO CI standards, policy, and process across all five pillars; embed CI requirements into GPO's procurement processes so impact activity is a defined, consistent step across every country rather than ad-hoc and local.

Regulations & Compliance — Own CI regulatory alignment and compliance across all 26 countries; maintain vetting and eligibility standards for NGOs, charities, suppliers, and partners with documented, auditable approval gates so CI activity routes through a compliant, risk-screened pathway.

Execution Excellence (incl. Waste to Worth & Donations) — Ensure quality and consistency of CI program execution across pillars and countries. Within this, lead GPO CI procurement donations (not supplier donations) end-to-end to a $10M 2027 target, and execute the Waste to Worth standard operating procedure (surplus and non-inventory product donations) globally.

Governance & Communication — Own the CI governance cadence: embed CI performance, standards, and compliance into Monthly Business Review and Quarterly Business Review forums, and run the communication plan that keeps Global Procurement Sustainability leadership, GPO leadership, and country stakeholders aligned on CI strategy and targets.

A day in the life
The Community Impact Excellence & Standards role is the owner of excellence, standards, and governance for the full GPO Community Impact (CI) team. The role brings strategy, policy, standards, regulatory, compliance, execution, and governance discipline across all five CI pillars: Supplier for Good, Procurement for Good, Waste to Worth, Space for Good / GPO Donation Hubs, and IDonate — globally across 26 countries.

This role makes CI consistent, compliant, measurable, and world-class: setting the standards and standard operating procedures that define how CI is executed everywhere, ensuring regulatory and recipient/partner compliance, raising execution quality, and building the governance and reporting that make CI impact visible to leadership.

Within this remit, the role also leads and owns GPO CI procurement donations end-to-end — not supplier donations — globally across 26 countries, including the Waste to Worth standard operating procedure and its execution, with a target of $10M in donations for 2027. Donations and Waste to Worth are a flagship execution stream inside the broader excellence-and-standards mandate.

The outcome is a Community Impact function that is standardized, compliant by design, regulation-aligned, executed to target, and measurable — and able to demonstrate the link between procurement activity and community sentiment toward Amazon, and ultimately the Profit & Loss

title: Software Development Engineer, Promotions Calculations Lifecycle (PCL)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon’s Worldwide Deals and Promotions organization builds the systems that compute and apply promotional benefits to hundreds of millions of customer orders every day. The Promotions Calculations Lifecycle (PCL) team owns the checkout-time calculation path: deciding which promotions apply to a cart, how benefits combine, and what the customer ultimately pays — correctly, at low latency, and at worldwide scale.

We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II (SDE II) to own the design, build, and operation of services on this critical path. You will work on high-throughput, low-latency systems where correctness is customer-facing and measured in real money. This is a hands-on engineering role for a builder who enjoys deep technical ownership, solving ambiguous problems with team members, and raising the operational bar for services that must work worldwide on Day 1.

Key job responsibilities
- Own end to end the design, implementation, testing, deployment, and operation of components and services on the promotions calculation path, from design document through post-launch monitoring.
- Design and build scalable, low-latency services and features that compute promotional benefits correctly at checkout for customers worldwide.
- Raise code quality through thorough, timely code reviews, strong testing practices, and secure, maintainable, well-instrumented code.
- Drive operational excellence — participate in on-call, reduce operational load through automation, and constructively identify and fix sources of defects and toil.
- Collaborate across teams with partner engineering teams, product managers, and stakeholders to deliver cross-functional initiatives that span multiple months.
- Work through ambiguity by breaking down loosely defined problems, unblocking yourself and others, and making pragmatic decisions that move the team forward.
- Mentor and uplevel peers and newer engineers through design feedback, pairing, and knowledge sharing.

A day in the life
A typical week combines focused building with the collaboration and operational rigor that keep a Tier-1 service healthy. You might start the day reviewing a design document for a change to how benefits combine at checkout, then pair with a teammate on the Universal Benefit Service (UBS) to reduce calculation latency on a high-traffic path. You will write and review code, add tests and metrics, and ship changes through the team’s continuous deployment pipeline.

You will take part in the on-call rotation for services the team owns, using operational signals to find and remove recurring sources of defects and toil. You will work with partner teams across Worldwide Deals and Promotions, and with product managers, to turn ambiguous requirements into concrete designs. You will also invest in the people around you — giving design feedback, mentoring newer engineers, and sharing what you learn so the whole team levels up.

About the team
The Promotions Calculations Lifecycle (PCL) team sits within Amazon’s Worldwide Deals and Promotions organization. We own the checkout-time path that determines which promotions apply to a customer’s cart, how those benefits combine, and the final price the customer pays. Our services run worldwide and are on the critical ordering path, so correctness, availability, and latency are first-order requirements — the systems we build directly shape both the customer experience and Amazon’s financials.

We are a team of builders who value deep technical ownership, operational excellence, and raising the bar for one another. We invest in mentorship and career growth, work backwards from the customer, and take pride in making complex systems simpler and more reliable over time. You will join a group where your work is highly visible, your decisions matter, and there is ample room to grow as an engineer.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Sr. Associate - Quality Analyst, Global Solutions & Risk Compliance (GSRC)
descriptionHtml:
The Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) organization is a component of Amazon's operations, dedicated to ensuring the compliance of its products and services worldwide. GSRC's core mission is to keep customers, partners, and associates safe while protecting the company from legal and regulatory risks. With a diverse global team spanning across India, China, Poland, Romania, Netherlands, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica, GSRC partners with its stakeholders to classify products and ensure regulatory and legal compliance for product listings. GSRC raises the bar on quality by implementing operational changes matching the everchanging regulatory space. The team designs global, consistent, and scalable solutions and prioritize a blend between technology-driven and human decision-making processes. GSRC believes that innovation thrives on diversity, fostering an inclusive and equitable culture that empowers employees with opportunities for learning and development.

Key job responsibilities
Your job responsibilities as a Sr. Compliance Associate-Quality Analyst may include:
• Performs quality audits on a daily basis using Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and achieves self-utilization, productivity and quality as per defined targets.
• Must be able to comprehend SOPs with minimal support and identify opportunities.
• Identifies anomalies through audits (SOP defects, Process gaps etc.).
• Uses knowledge and identifies defect/s & preliminary root causes, explains the rationale
• Proposes solutions on quality/productivity and work on milestones with managers
• Expertise in research – finding specific information (eg: products, regulations etc) in a timely manner.
• Prepares key insight trends and share reports on regular basis.
• Provide feedbacks to the associates and close loop on audit observations.
• Respond to stakeholders with guidance and flags any updates to Lead/Manager

About the team
Amazon is an E-commerce and Cloud Computing company with headquarters in Seattle, Washington. Since 1995, Amazon has focused on being “the world’s most customer centric company.” Our customers are worldwide, and include not just consumers, but also our sellers and vendors (selling partners). World-class retail brands and individual sellers increase their sales and reach new customers by leveraging the power of the Amazon e-commerce platform. To meet our selling partners’ needs, our smart, diverse, customer-obsessed employees are constantly innovating and building on new ideas.
The Operational Risk Compliance (ORC) organization exists to keep our customers and partners safe, protect associates, and ensure legal and regulatory compliance. We coordinate the aspects of product transactions that are regulated (distribution, shipping, sale, and import/export). Global Solutions and Risk Compliance (GSRC) is the operational arm of the ORC organization. This involves analyzing product import documentation and flagging hazardous risks. We are also responsible for keeping Amazon customers safe and informed by coordinating actions around worldwide program teams to classify products and ensure Amazon’s product listings follow regulatory and legal compliance guidelines. These actions include removing products from the site and from our warehouses, and contacting customers with pertinent sustainability information. The ORC team partners with GSRC supports regulatory compliance requirements for Amazon’s worldwide programs such as Dangerous Goods, Chemical Safety Compliance, Global Trade Services, Transport Risk Compliance, Sustainability, Extended Producer Responsibility and Food Safety. GSRC has offices across India, China, Poland, Romania, Jordan, Philippines and Costa Rica and supports compliance related needs for worldwide Amazon marketplaces.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree
- 1+ years of logistics, transportation, supply chain, import/export operations, or data entry/data administration experience
- Knowledge of Excel at a basic level (e.g., UX navigation, math & logical functions, lookup functions, etc.)
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Work 40 hours/week, and overtime as required
- Experience performing accurate data entry and analysis

Preferred qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Bachelor's degree in logistics, transporation, supply chain, or business
- Licensed customs broker
- Experience in international logistics, cross-border transportation and supply chain, or U.S. Customs rules and regulations
- Experience in customs

title: Design and Construction Quality Manager, Design & Construction
descriptionHtml:
Would you like an opportunity to travel and work regionally? The role will be based in either Brazil or Mexico with up to 50% of time travelling either domestically or to other EMEA countries.

Amazon opened its doors in 1995 and strives to be the world's most customer-centric company, where customers can find and discover anything they might want to buy online.

Join our Design and Construction team as a Quality Manager and play a pivotal role in shaping project success from concept to completion. In this dynamic position, you'll drive excellence across the entire project lifecycle by establishing robust Quality, Commissioning and Turnover management processes that seamlessly integrate across all construction phases—from preconstruction through execution, commissioning, qualification, and go-live/handover.

As a strategic partner to cross-functional teams, you'll develop and implement a planned and structured delivery approach that begins during the early project stages and seamlessly progresses through Preconstruction, Execution, Commissioning, Qualification, and Turnover phases. You'll ensure quality standards are embedded throughout each phase, creating a cohesive handover process that sets our facilities up for operational excellence. This role offers the flexibility to adapt your approach based on project needs while maintaining a relentless focus on quality outcomes and successful facility transitions.

Key job responsibilities
• Lead quality management systems and KPI tracking across commissioning and turnover phases for regional project portfolio with periodic performance reviews
• Develop detailed execution plans for testing activities, manage schedules and budgets, and coordinate vendor representatives and resource requirements
• Deploy electronic turnover databases, oversee documentation processes, and ensure receipt of O&M manuals, training materials, and engineering databases
• Conduct progressive contractor audits to verify compliance with project, industry, and regulatory requirements throughout construction and commissioning
• Collaborate with Construction, RME, Operations, Design, and support teams to define turnover philosophy and resolve technical issues
• Drive contractor progress to completion, organize final system walkdowns, create risk-based punch lists, and verify completion of critical items
• Coordinate detailed area commissioning plans, inspect construction completion status, establish safety procedures, and monitor priority work areas

Your day begins supporting execution teams to deliver projects, working alongside construction managers, technical specialists, and contractors to resolve quality challenges on-site and ensure compliance with standards. You'll conduct inspections across mechanical, electrical, and structural systems, coach team members on quality processes, and facilitate seamless coordination between design, construction, and operations stakeholders. Using data and performance insights, you'll drive continuous improvement by analyzing trends in commissioning progress, defect patterns, and turnover documentation. This analysis informs tactical initiatives to refine quality management systems and enhance processes from preconstruction through final handover. Collaboration spans cross-functional teams, including procurement, cost, compliance, and technical vendor management, ensuring quality excellence throughout the project lifecycle and successful facility transitions to operations.

About the team
The D&C Quality team drives excellence across Amazon's global design and construction portfolio. We partner with cross-functional stakeholders—including RME, construction, operations, procurement, and technical specialists—to embed quality standards throughout the project lifecycle. Our team spans multiple International countries, combining hands-on execution support with data-driven insights to continuously improve processes, mentor emerging talent, and ensure seamless facility transitions. We're committed to delivering world-class infrastructure that meets Amazon's operational excellence standards while fostering innovation in construction quality management.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Construction Management or an equivalent engineering science
- Experience in managing technical teams with significant personnel management experience and examples of developing engineers and building successful teams
- Experience gathering and analyzing large amounts of data and delivering continuous business improvements
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English at C1 level or above
- Professional experience in a commissioning or quality management role, including completions and commissioning of complex installations to effectively lead, supervise, and resolve execution issues on a day-to-day basis
- Management, influence, and communications skills to establish and communicate the systems required for successful execution of the commissioning and turnover scope
- Contractual and technical experience, as well as a solid foundation in project completion management practices
- Experience developing and implementing quality management systems across multiple projects

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in budgeting, scheduling and technical workflows
- Experience using data and metrics to drive improvements
- Experience with database management systems
- Functional knowledge of all project discipline systems, design and reporting processes
- Working knowledge of design review and reporting technologies

title: ICQA Area Manager - Amazon Now, 3PL ICQA Team
descriptionHtml:
Do you have a Bias for Action?

Would you like to be part of an innovative, fast-paced and motivated team?

We’re glad to hear it.

Each action we undertake is on behalf of our customers, which is why we keep a close eye on all processes in our Fulfillment Centers. Our Fulfillment Centers are at the heart of Amazon’s world-class and rapidly growing Operations network: they’re where we manage our fast-moving inventory. They’re also where we developed our industry-leading workflows. Our teams stow deliveries, pick products, package them up and ship them out.

We’re looking for a detail-oriented leader to join our Inventory Control and Quality Assurance team. We’ll need you to ensure that we continue delivering as reliably as ever to our customers, with all teams maintaining their performance and quality of service.

When working on Inventory Control (IC), you’ll carry out extensive analysis and research, as you come to understand and correct any vacancies in our inventory.

The other significant portion of your time will be devoted to Quality Assurance (QA). In this line of responsibility, you’ll proactively audit team efficiency. For example: how closely everyone in your Fulfillment Center is adhering to agreed processes, while highlighting any discrepancies.

Key job responsibilities
- Managing the site-based Inventory Control and Quality Assurance team,
- You’ll maintain Health and Safety standards within your sphere of influence, actively promoting a positive Health and Safety culture on-site,
- Monitor KPIs regarding accuracy and integrity of Quality and Inventory transactions; then, you’ll provide feedback to Operations where necessary,
- Review and analyze customer defect data, while developing corresponding action plans to reduce and eliminate causes of any issues,
- On a daily, weekly and monthly basis: develop and execute action plans for increasing quality, inventory accuracy and service satisfaction,
- Partner with Management in the communication of Inventory Control and Quality Assurance policies and procedures: you’ll keep an eye on compliance in your Fulfillment Center,
- Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with Amazon’s wider policies and procedures, including:
- Interviewing and training both exempt and non-exempt employees,
- Assuming accountability for setting and meeting operational goals,
- Planning and forecasting,
- Assigning and directing work and employee deliverables,
- Performance appraisal of team members,
- Rewarding and disciplining employees where appropriate.
- To build up an understanding of Fulfillment Center inventory systems and processes, and to provide assistance and expertise for problem-solving wherever you can.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience developing experimental and analytic plans for data modeling processes, use of strong baselines, ability to accurately determine cause and effect relations
- Experience managing multiple projects and priorities across teams in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
- Experience communicating with a wide range of stakeholders, including colleagues and leadership, or experience managing teams
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English, and have the ability to take direction in English
- Bachelor's degree in mathematics, engineering, statistics, computer science, business administration or a related field
- Work flexible hours as business demands, including overnight, weekends and holidays
- Willing to travel between cities in EG to accommodate quick commerce site visits (Travel between cities is expansible in terms of fuel/transportation & hotel accommodation)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience within a distribution center, logistics, or manufacturing environment
- Knowledge of Six Sigma tools and Lean techniques
